Amen.

Its pairing of "temporal" with "signifieth" and "everlasting" recalls the Corpus Christi
postcommunion "Grant us, we beseech thee, O Lord, to be filled with the everlasting enjoyment of thy Godhead, which the temporal receiving of thy precious Body and Blood doth prefigure". It may be a free reworking
of it; this is a suggestion, not Sehling's identification. Mecklenburg took Döber's prayer into
its list of three.

**Mecklenburg's three.** Mecklenburg 1545 offers all three kinds: Luther's, Döber's, and the
Corpus Christi collect. **Mecklenburg, *Ordeninge der misse*, 1545** (Sehling 5, p. 155):

<!-- doc 1922 -->

Thereupon the priest: Let us pray. We give thanks unto thee, Almighty Lord God, that thou hast
refreshed us through this salutary gift of thy body and blood; and we beseech thy mercy, that
thou wouldest make the same to prosper in us unto strong faith toward thee and unto fervent love
among us all; through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen. Or at times this prayer: O Lord, almighty
Father, grant us in our minds and hearts that, through the temporal death of thy Son, which this
worthy mystery signifieth, we may trust that thou hast given us everlasting life; through Jesus
Christ our Lord. Amen. Or this: O thou dear Lord God, who by this wonderful sacrament hast
commanded us to remember and to preach thy passion; grant us so to use this sacrament of thy
body and blood, that we may daily perceive in us fruitfully thy redemption; through Jesus
Christ. Amen.

**(e) Alternating Sundays: Prussia 1544.** The Prussian order of 1544 has two postcommunions
sung "to alternate every other Sunday". The second is a new prayer on the fruit of the passion.
**Prussia, *Kirchenordnung*, 1544** (Sehling 4, p. 66):

<!-- doc 1833 -->

Thereafter the priest turneth to the people and singeth: The Lord be with you; and turneth again
to the altar, [and] singeth one of the collects with the customary accent, etc., to alternate
every other Sunday. First collect: We give thanks unto thee, etc. […] Another collect: O true
God, merciful Father, we heartily beseech thee, let us needy ones rightly lay hold with
believing heart on the profit and fruit of the holy passion of our Lord, that is, grace and the
forgiveness of our sins, even as through the word of thy holy Son we have truly received under
the bread and wine his holy body and his precious blood, which he gave and shed for us; through
the same our Lord Jesus Christ, thy Son, who liveth and reigneth with thee from everlasting to
everlasting. Amen.

The Prussian articles of 1525 had already provided "two common collects or complendas for the
end of the Mass, to alternate through the whole year". Sehling does not print them
(Sehling 4, p. 37).

**(f) Later replacements.** Late orders sometimes replace Luther's short prayer with a longer
one. At Engerhafe in East Frisia (1583) "a trinitarian thanksgiving has taken the place of
Luther's short thanksgiving collect (postcommunion)", as Sehling's editor notes in comparing it
with the order of 1535 (Sehling 7/1, p. 681, n. 34). The thanksgiving with the *Placeat* in
Kantz's Mass of 1522 is treated in [Chapter 7](#ch7),
[§7.2.7](#s7-2-7).

#### <a id="s5-6-5"></a>5.6.5 When there was no communion

**A collect instead.** Without communicants the Lutheran Mass ended after the sermon, and the
postcommunion slot was filled with "a collect" of the pastor's choice, not with the thanksgiving
for the sacrament:
- **Saxony 1580**: "But where no communicants are present, it shall be concluded after the
  sermon, or a chapter of Holy Scripture read, with a Christian collect and the customary
  blessing" (Sehling 1, p. 369).
- **Soest 1609**: "When there are no communicants, the preacher may conclude with a collect of
  his own choice" (*arbitraria collecta*, Sehling 22, p. 495).
- **Lippe 1571**: a collect "or thanksgiving for the word of God heard". **Lippe,
  *Kirchenordnung*, 1571** (Sehling 21, p. 397):

<!-- doc 1462 -->

Thereupon sing a collect or thanksgiving for the word of God which hath been heard, and conclude
with a Christian hymn.

The thanksgiving for the gift of the sacrament became, in the service without communion, a
thanksgiving for the gift of the Word.

The service when nobody communicated is treated in [Chapter 2](#ch2),
[§2.14](#s2-14), and the Litany sung in place of the Mass in
[Chapter 13](#ch13), [§13.22.1](#s13-22-1).

#### <a id="s5-6-6"></a>5.6.6 The prayer over the people (*oratio super populum*)

**The medieval use.** On the weekdays of Lent the Missal added a fourth proper prayer after the
postcommunion. The deacon bade the people *Humiliate capita vestra Deo*, "Bow down your heads
before God", and the priest said the *oratio super populum*, a prayer over the people, before
the dismissal. In the Breviary the same prayers served as collects of the office on the Lenten
weekdays.

**Not at the Mass.** No Lutheran order in the corpus keeps the *super populum* (over the people) at the end of the
Mass. The bidding *Humiliate capita vestra Deo* does not occur, in Latin or in German. The
corpus was searched for *super populum*, *super plebem* (over the people), *humiliate capita* (bow your heads), *inclinate capita* (incline your heads)
and German phrases such as "neiget eure Häupter" (bow your heads). The Lutheran Mass had no weekday Lenten Masses
to carry the prayer. Its place at the end of the Sunday Mass was held by the postcommunion
collect and the Aaronic blessing. The orders describe that blessing in the same words: "the
blessing over the people out of the book of Numbers"
(Gnandstein 1539, Sehling 1, p. 564). Müntzer
(Radical Reformation) describes his postcommunion the same way: "after the communion one giveth
thanks to God over the people, and blesseth the Lord" (Sehling 1, p. 506). Neither is a *super
populum* prayer.

**In the office: Ansbach 1533.** The one place where the *super populum* survives by name is in
the Divine Office of the collegiate churches. The Brandenburg-Ansbach order of 1533 for the
singing and reading in the *Stifte* goes through the Breviary and strikes out what is unfit. In
Lent it strikes out the collects at Lauds (*super Benedictus*) that "speak of the fast" as a
work, day by day. For their place it allows the *super populum* prayers.
**Brandenburg-Ansbach-Kulmbach, *Ordnung singens und lesens bei den Stiften*, 1533**
(Sehling 11, p. 315):

<!-- doc 276 -->

On Ash Wednesday the collect at the Benedictus, *Concede nobis, Domine, praesidia* (Grant us, O Lord, the protection), and other
collects more which speak of the fast, as *Inchoata ieiunia* (The fasts begun) and *Adesto, Domine,
supplicationibus nostris* (Be present, O Lord, at our supplications), etc., and the hymn *Ex more docti* (Taught by custom), shall not be kept. Further they
shall leave out: on the Sunday Invocavit, the collect at the Benedictus *Deus, qui ecclesiam
tuam* (O God, who [dost cleanse] thy church); […] on the Monday after Reminiscere, the collect at the Benedictus *Praesta, quaesumus,
omnipotens Deus, familia tua* (Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, [that] thy household), etc.; on the Wednesday, the collect at the Benedictus *Populum
tuum, Domine* (Thy people, O Lord), etc.; on the Thursday, the collect at the Benedictus *Praesta nobis, Domine,
quaesumus* (Grant us, O Lord, we beseech thee); on the Friday, at the Benedictus the collect *Da, quaesumus, omnipotens Deus* (Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God), etc.;
on the Saturday, at the Benedictus the collect *Da, quaesumus, Domine, nostris effectum* (Grant, we beseech thee, O Lord, to our [fasts] a saving effect); and in
this place they may always take the *super populum* that followeth.

**What the rule means.** The list goes on through the weeks of Oculi, Laetare and Judica
(Sehling 11, pp. 315–316).
- **What it strikes out.** The Lauds collects of the Lenten weekdays are the collects of the
  day's Mass. Many of them ask that bodily fasting be made fruitful or meritorious. An example
  is the Monday after Reminiscere: "Grant, we beseech thee, almighty God, that thy household, which by afflicting itself abstaineth from food in the flesh, may by following righteousness fast from sin". Another is the
  Wednesday: "Look mercifully, O Lord, upon thy people, and grant that those whom thou biddest abstain from carnal
foods may also cease from hurtful vices".
- **What it puts in their place.** "The *super populum* that followeth" is the prayer over the
  people of the same day, which stands after the postcommunion in the Missal. These prayers ask
  for God's protection, mercy and guidance of his people, without reference to the fast. For the
  same Monday it is "Be present, almighty God, at our supplications, and to those to whom thou grantest confidence of
hoping for thy goodness, graciously give the effect of thy wonted mercy".

The identification of these texts is this chapter's. Sehling's editor gives no note on the
passage.

**The result.** The Lenten prayer over the people outlived the Lenten collect in this one
Lutheran order. It did so not at the end of the Mass but at Lauds, and for a doctrinal reason:
of the day's two proper prayers it was the one that said nothing of fasting as a work. Ansbach's
handling matches Luther's test for the collect in 1523, "if only it be godly" ([§5.3.2](#s5-3-2)). The corpus
shows no other Lutheran use of the *super populum*.

### <a id="s5-7"></a>5.7 Kept, stripped, added, altered

**Table 1. The prayers, compared with the medieval system**

| | Collect | Secret | Postcommunion | Prayer over the people (Lent) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Medieval use** | Proper to the day; sung after the Gloria; multiplied by commemorations and votive collects | Proper to the day; said silently over the gifts; multiplied with the collects | Proper to the day; sung after the communion; multiplied with the collects | Proper to the Lenten weekdays; after the postcommunion, with the bidding *Humiliate capita vestra Deo*; also used as an office collect |
| **Kept** | The collect of the season or feast ([§5.4.2](#s5-4-2)), mostly German versions of the Missal collects; the salutation, *Oremus*, long conclusion and Amen ([§5.4.5](#s5-4-5)); the seasonal versicle (Henneberg 1582, Hof 1592) | Only the closing *Per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen* (World without end. Amen; Müntzer (Radical Reformation), Lippe, Calenberg-Göttingen), and the name in Dortmund 1554 ([§5.5.2](#s5-5-2)) | A collect after the communion, with salutation and Amen; often still called the *complenda* (completion; [§5.6.3](#s5-6-3)). Proper postcommunions kept in Nürnberg and Volprecht 1524, Coburg 1524, Müntzer 1524 (Radical Reformation), Erfurt 1525 and Calenberg-Göttingen 1542 ([§5.6.2](#s5-6-2)) | Only in the office: Ansbach 1533 allows the day's *super populum* (over the people) at Lauds ([§5.6.6](#s5-6-6)) |
| **Stripped** | Collects of the saints and those asking their intercession (Hannover 1536); the automatic commemorations (Luther: "that one alone") | The prayer itself, everywhere (Prussia 1525: "of necessity left out"); no German secret exists | The proper postcommunion (Luther 1523: "they almost all sound of sacrifice"); gone from the printed orders after 1542 | At the Mass, everywhere; neither the prayer nor the bidding occurs |
| **Added** | Veit Dietrich's gospel collects (Wolfenbüttel 1569, Soest 1609, Buxtehude 1565); new "common" collects for need; the collect for peace after *Verleih uns Frieden* (Grant us peace) | Open prayers for the magistrates and Christendom in its place (Dortmund 1554); collects for rulers under the Sanctus (Döber 1525, Brandenburg 1540, Calenberg-Göttingen 1542, Pfalz-Neuburg 1543) | Luther's fixed thanksgiving (1526); the Nürnberg thanksgiving (1533); Döber's prayer (1525); Prussia's second collect (1544); a collect or thanksgiving for the Word when there is no communion (Lippe 1571) | — |
| **Altered** | Latin to German "that the people may say Amen" (Coburg 1554/55); one collect as the norm, a second only "for need" (Mecklenburg 1545) or by rule for temporal goods (Ansbach 1548); the Advent *Excita* reworded ("awaken us, that we may be ready") | — | Proper to ordinary; Luther's 1523 ablution prayers made public, then expanded (Nürnberg 1533); the Missal postcommunion *Gratias tibi referimus* (We give thee thanks) recast as Luther's thanksgiving; the Corpus Christi collect turned into a postcommunion; two thanksgivings joined "under one conclusion" (Brandenburg 1540, Pfalz-Neuburg 1543) | Moved from the end of the Mass to Lauds, in place of collects that "speak of the fast" (Ansbach 1533) |

**Table 2. Did the medieval "two collects, two secrets, two postcommunions" survive?**

| Feature | Survives? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| More than one collect before the epistle | **Yes, in some orders** | Ansbach 1548 (two, by rule); Mecklenburg 1545 (a second "for need"); Wolfstein 1574 and Henneberg ("one or more") |
| A matching second secret | **No** | The secret is gone altogether |
| A matching second postcommunion | **No, but two postcommunions do occur**, not tied to the collects | Brandenburg 1540 and Pfalz-Neuburg 1543 (Nürnberg and Luther thanksgivings "under one conclusion"); Calenberg-Göttingen 1542 (Luther's thanksgiving plus the proper postcommunion of the feast) |
| A votive prayer at the end | **Yes** | The collect for peace after *Verleih uns Frieden* (twelve or more orders); Hof 1592's collect "for rain and fair weather" |
| Rules for the conclusions | **Yes** | Hof 1592 ([§5.4.5](#s5-4-5)) |
| The Lenten prayer over the people | **Not at the Mass**; once in the office | Ansbach 1533, at Lauds ([§5.6.6](#s5-6-6)) |

## <a id="ch6"></a>Chapter 6. The General Prayer of the Church: Texts by Family


The general prayer (*das gemein Gebet*, the Prayer of the Church) is the intercession for all
estates and needs in the chief Sunday service of the church orders in the Sehling corpus. This
chapter does two things:

- §§[6.1](#s6-1)–[6.3](#s6-3) say what the general prayer is, where it stands in the service, and how its texts are
  related.
- §§[6.4](#s6-4)–[6.21](#s6-21) give the texts themselves, one family at a time. For each petition the original is
  followed by the English, for the rubric, the bid and the prayer in turn. Each family can be
  read straight through, in the order in which the prayer runs.

The texts are the **representative texts** of the general-prayer workbook,
`general_prayers.xlsx` ([Introduction](#repo-prayers)). They come from four sheets of the workbook:

- **Orig Prayers - Representative**;
- **Eng Prayers - Representative**;
- **Orig Bids - Representative**;
- **Eng Bids - Representative**.

The workbook sets these out with one row per category and one column per family, so that one
intention can be compared across the families. Here they are turned around: each family's column
is printed as a single prayer.

The Introduction ([The general-prayer workbook and database](#repo-prayers)) describes the
workbook and `general_prayers.db`: how the texts were curated and checked against the corpus,
the categories, and how the critical and representative texts are made. The workbook also gives:

- every witness's own text, in the **Prayers** sheet;
- the variants within a family, in the **Archetypes** sheet and the critical sheets;
- the orders side by side, petition by petition, in the **Compare** sheet.

**Related chapters.** Several subjects are treated more fully elsewhere:
- the place of the general prayer in the order of the Mass:
  [Chapter 2](#ch2), §§[2.4](#s2-4)–[2.5](#s2-5);
- the prayer before the sermon, the greeting and the notices:
  [Chapter 11](#ch11), [§11.10](#s11-10);
- the Litany and the bidding prayers:
  [Chapter 13](#ch13), [§13.22](#s13-22);
- the intercessions under the Sanctus in the Masses that have them:
  [Chapter 7](#ch7), §§[7.8.11](#s7-8-11), [7.12.2](#s7-12-2), [7.14.4](#s7-14-4);
- the collects: [Chapter 5](#ch5), [§5.4](#s5-4).

The labels of the texts (rubric, bid, prayer and witnesses) are explained in the
[Conventions](#conv-quotations).

### <a id="s6-1"></a>6.1 The general prayer in the Sunday service

#### <a id="s6-1-1"></a>6.1.1 What it is

Every order in this set (57 witnesses, dated 1526–1618) has one prayer in the chief service of
the Sunday in which the congregation prays for the Church and her ministers, the magistrates,
the afflicted and the other needs of Christendom. The orders call it:

- *das gemein gebet*, the common prayer. This is the usual name: Württemberg 1553 has "Ordnung
  des gemeinen gebets" (Order of the common prayer), Leipzig 1567 "Gemein gebet" (Common prayer).
- *Vermanung zum gebet*, the exhortation to prayer: Hessen 1566 (Moderate Reformed), Strasbourg
  1598. Nürnberg 1545 has "Vermanung zu bitten für allerlei stende" (Exhortation to pray for all estates).
- *Fürbitt* (intercession) or *Vorbitt*, intercession: Augsburg 1537 (Moderate Reformed; Sehling's heading),
  Öhringen 1544.
- *Exhortatio edder vormaninge*, exhortation or admonition: Braunschweig 1528, Hamburg 1529.
- *Oratio* (Prayer): the Latin order of the French church at Frankfurt, 1554 (Reformed).

Hessen 1566 (Moderate Reformed) gives it as the fifth part of the service and grounds it in the
practice of the first Church:

> Of such prayer, which in the first Church followed upon the exposition of the Scripture and
> the sermon, Justin speaketh very briefly in his second Apology, where he saith: *After the
> exhortations made by him that presideth, we all rise and pray together*; that is, when the
> sermon of the chief teacher is ended, we all stand up and pray.

What counts as the general prayer, and what is left out (collect banks, the Litany, prayer-day
and afternoon forms), is set out in the Introduction
([What counts as the general prayer](#repo-prayers-scope)).

#### <a id="s6-1-2"></a>6.1.2 Where it stands in the service

**After the sermon.** In 48 of the 57 witnesses the prayer follows the sermon, and in most of
them it is said from the pulpit. Kursachsen 1580 has it said "always after the sermon … to the people from the pulpit". In these orders
the prayer is the hinge between the service of the Word and the Supper, and it is often joined
to the items around it:

- **Before it, in many orders:** an open confession and absolution, or the publishing of banns
  and notices. Examples:
  - confession and absolution in Neckarbischofsheim 1560, Erbach 1560, Hohenlohe 1578, the
    Ysenburg orders, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569, Oldenburg 1573 and Kurpfalz 1563
    (Reformed);
  - banns and notices in Hohenlohe 1578, Solms-Laubach 1576, Strasbourg 1598 and Frankfurt 1554
    (Reformed).
- **After it:** the Our Father, which closes almost every form. Then:
  - a psalm or hymn, such as "Erhalt uns Herr" (Keep us, Lord), "Verleih uns Frieden" (Grant us peace) or "Danck sagen wir alle" (Let us all give thanks);
  - a collect and the blessing when there is no Communion;
  - otherwise the Supper. In Lüneburg 1564 and its followers the communicants come into the
    choir and kneel.

**Elsewhere in the service.** The other nine witnesses place it as follows:

| Place | Witnesses |
|---|---|
| In the Mass, said by the priest in German under the Sanctus, before or after the Words of Institution | Brandenburg 1540, Calenberg-Göttingen 1542, Pfalz-Neuburg 1543 (family L) |
| In the Communion office, after the exhortation to the communicants, before the Words of Institution | Frankfurt 1553 and 1589 |
| After the Kyrie and Gloria, in place of the Latin collect, read from a lectern before the altar (the sermon precedes the whole service) | Schwäbisch Hall 1526 |
| In place of the Epistle in the village Mass, followed by the Creed, the Ten Commandments and the catechism (the medieval pulpit office) | Nürnberg 1545 |
| After the Gospel has been expounded from the pulpit and the catechism recited, before the Creed and Preface | Osnabrück 1543 |
| From the pulpit, when the choir has finished the first psalm or hymn | Worms 1560 |

The Brandenburg prayers keep the place of the old intercessions of the Canon. Sehling notes on
Pfalz-Neuburg 1543:

> These prayers are set in the place of the intercessory prayers spoken in the Roman Mass partly
> before and partly after the consecration. Elsewhere in the evangelical church orders these
> were struck out without replacement, because they rest upon the sacrificial character of the
> Mass, which the Reformation rejected.

**Who says it.** The minister says it: the pastor or the deacon from the pulpit, or the priest
at the altar in family L. In Schwäbisch Hall 1526 it is read from a lectern before the altar, in
a cope. The people take part:

- by saying the Our Father;
- by the confession, which they say after the minister in Braunschweig ("say ye also the confession with me") and in Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582 ("Confess with me your sins before God");
- by praying "with mouth and heart", as the Leipzig print of 1567 directs.

#### <a id="s6-1-3"></a>6.1.3 Its forms

The witnesses use six forms. Each family keeps to one form, except for the two prescriptions of
contents: Magdeburg 1562 (in B2) and Osnabrück 1543 (in H).

| Form | How it runs | Families | Witnesses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bidding and collect | For each intention the minister bids the people ("Let us pray for …"), then says a collect | A, B1 | 10 |
| Bidding exhortation | The minister tells the people what to pray for, item by item, without addressing God, and closes with the Our Father | C, D, G, H, I, J, M | 14 |
| Continuous prayer | One prayer to God that names the intentions in turn ("Wouldest thou also …") | B2, E, F, R1, R3, R4 | 25 |
| Collects | Separate collects without biddings: three from the pulpit (K), or the priest's collects under the Sanctus (L) | K, L | 4 |
| Lord's Prayer paraphrase | The intentions are arranged under the petitions of the Our Father | R2 (and the close of R3) | 2 |
| Prescription of contents | Not a text to be read, but a list in indirect speech of what the prayer must contain | Magdeburg 1562 (B2), Osnabrück 1543 (H) | 2 |

**Long and short forms.** Württemberg 1553 prints a long form (B1) and a short form (B2).
Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557 says when each is to be used:

> This prayer, forasmuch as it is somewhat long, the ministers of the Church may use at the
> great feasts, as on Christmas Day, Easter and Pentecost, and at any other time in the year
> when the church is not otherwise held long by the sermon; else they shall commonly read to the
> people the shorter form, which followeth hereafter.

The short form became the most copied prayer in the corpus (17 witnesses, 1553–1618).

**Alternatives and freedom.** Some orders allow the prayer to vary:

- **The Litany instead.** The Litany is the second form of the common prayer in Württemberg 1553
  and Rothenburg 1559. It is prayed on Fridays in the towns of Kursachsen 1580 and on alternate
  Sundays in Rothenberg 1618.
- **A choice of texts.** Kurpfalz 1563 (Reformed) offers a Lord's-Prayer paraphrase, "Or thus"
  (or thus), beside its Sunday prayer (R2). Augsburg 1537 (Moderate Reformed) offers two texts
  against the Turk.
- **Local adaptation.**
  - Hessen 1566 (Moderate Reformed) lets each church make the form "shorter or longer".
  - Hanau-Lichtenberg 1573 tells the pastor to refer to the sermon and to present needs.
  - Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588 (Reformed) lets ministers add to the prayer in time of need.
  - Many forms end with a rubric that lets the sick and other particular needs be named (the
    category *Special intercessions*).

#### <a id="s6-1-4"></a>6.1.4 The sequence of intentions

**Lutheran.** The usual Lutheran series goes back to Brenz 1526 and Württemberg 1553:

exhortation > Church > magistrates > afflicted > peace > enemies > women with child > fruits of
the earth > Our Father.

**Reformed.** The Heidelberg prayer of 1563 begins with confession and thanksgiving, prays for
the fruit of the Word, and has a petition for all men (1 Tim 2:1):

confession > thanksgiving > Word > magistrates > fruits of the earth > all men > persecuted >
afflicted > Our Father.

**What all share.** Civil authority is the one intention found in every witness.
The Introduction ([What the comparison shows](#repo-prayers-findings)) sets out the other patterns.

**Traditions.**

The traditions follow the inventory in [Chapter 1](#ch1), [§1.3](#s1-3).
Every order of another tradition than the Lutheran is marked where it is cited, by its tradition
in brackets after it, as "Kurpfalz 1563 (Reformed)".
- Eleven families are Lutheran: A to E and H to L.
- F (Augsburg 1537) is Moderate Reformed: Upper German and Bucerian.
- G (Hessen 1566) is Moderate Reformed: the church of Philip of Hesse, between Wittenberg and
  the Upper Germans, which bore Bucer's stamp.
- M (Norden 1528) is an early East Frisian evangelical order, which Sehling prints among the
  Reformed orders of East Frisia; it is marked Reformed here.
- R1–R4 are Reformed. Schaumburg 1614, a Lutheran order, takes over the Heidelberg prayer of R1.
- No Interim order is among the witnesses.

### <a id="s6-2"></a>6.2 How the texts are given here

**Representative texts.** A family's representative text is one clean text for each category,
made from all the family's witnesses by majority:

- a petition, bid or prayer is kept if at least half the witnesses to that category have it;
- word by word, the reading of the majority is chosen;
- where no reading has half the witnesses, the earliest witness's reading stands.

Every word comes from a witness, but in a family with several witnesses the result need not
match any one witness exactly. Where a family has a single witness, its text is that witness's
text. The rules are given in full in the Introduction ([Representative texts](#repo-prayers-rules)).

**Order.** The workbook lists the categories in a standard order. Here each family's petitions
follow the order in which its prayer actually runs:

- the order of the family's earliest witness;
- with petitions that only later witnesses have placed where those witnesses have them.

Where a family has more than one petition in a category (two petitions for the magistrates in
Lüneburg 1564, or the confession and the absolution), the workbook cell holds them both,
separated by a blank line. Here each is given in its own place.

**Exact reproduction.** The petitions of each family, joined category by category, reproduce the
four workbook sheets exactly. This was checked for all 2,016 cells (28 categories × 18 families
× 4 sheets), with no differences. The workbook's "Bids" sheets put the rubric on the first line
of the bid; here the rubric and the bid are given separately.

**Each petition** is numbered within its family (A.1, A.2, …) and headed with its category. For
families with more than one witness, a line in italics names the witnesses that have the
petition. It also notes where a rubric, bid or prayer is in only some of them. Then come, in
turn:

- the rubric, original then English;
- the bid, original then English;
- the prayer, original then English.

Each part is given only where the petition has it.

**Not taken in.** Each family section lists the witness petitions that are not in the
representative text, because another reading of the same category has the majority. Those texts
are in the **Prayers** sheet and in the critical sheets.

in the representative text given below.

| [C](#s6-7) | Bidding exhortation (Strasbourg type) | Lutheran | German | bidding exhortation + Our Father | 1 | 1573 | 8 |

### <a id="s6-4"></a>6.4 Family A: Brenz bidding prayer

Deacon or pastor bids the people for one intention ("Let us pray for …"), then says a
collect for it; the series runs Church, magistrates, peace, afflicted, all needs, and closes
with the Lord's Prayer. Frankfurt adds collects from Brandenburg-Nürnberg 1533 and Veit
Dietrich.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Schwäbisch Hall 1526 (Brenz).
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** bidding + collect.
- **Place in the service (Schwäbisch Hall 1526):** After the Kyrie and Gloria, in place of the
  Latin Oremus/collect; read from a lectern before the altar in a cope. The sermon precedes the
  whole service.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1526 | Schwäbisch Hall, Frühmessordnung (Johannes Brenz) | Schwäbisch Hall (Imperial city) | Sehling 17, I/1, pp. 37–40 | bidding + collect |
| 1543 | Schwäbisch Hall, Kirchenordnung 1543 | Schwäbisch Hall (Imperial city) | Sehling 17, I/10, pp. 142–145 | bidding + collect |
| 1553 | Frankfurt am Main, Agende 1553 („Einfeltige form, das Nachtmal des Herren zuhalten“) | Frankfurt am Main (Imperial city) | Sehling 9, VI/Frankfurt Nr. 10, pp. 524–526 | bidding + collect |
| 1560 | Neckarbischofsheim, Kirchenordnung (Herren von Helmstatt) | Lordship of Neckarbischofsheim (Kraichgau) | Sehling 16, V, pp. 670–672 | bidding + collect |
| 1589 | Frankfurt am Main, Agende 1589 | Frankfurt am Main (Imperial city) | Sehling 9, VI/Frankfurt Nr. 13, pp. 552–553 | bidding + collect |

The representative text follows Brenz's Schwäbisch Hall form of 1526, which the later witnesses
copy with small changes. Where they part from it, as in the preface and the close, its reading
stands. Following the family's own majority, each bid ends "Bittend also:" (Pray ye thus:) and the collects end
bare (see the Introduction, [Representative texts](#repo-prayers-rules), rule 4).

A.9 to A.13 (the Our Father, Creed and Decalogue printed as part of the prayer, and the closing
rubric) stand in Schwäbisch Hall 1526 (A.9 also in 1543). A.14 is Frankfurt 1589's own closing
prayer for the communicants and A.15 Neckarbischofsheim 1560's closing word of assurance. They
come at the end, after the Our Father, as in those orders.

**Not in the representative text** (a minority reading of its category; see the Prayers sheet or
the critical sheets): Frankfurt 1553 no. 1 (Exhortation / preface); Frankfurt 1553 no. 7 (Lord's
Prayer); Neckarbischofsheim 1560 no. 1 (Exhortation / preface); Neckarbischofsheim 1560 no. 9
(Lord's Prayer); Frankfurt 1589 no. 1 (Exhortation / preface); Frankfurt 1589 no. 7 (Lord's
Prayer).

**Sequence:** A.1 Exhortation / preface > A.2 The Church > A.3 Civil authority > A.4 The
afflicted > A.5 Peace > A.6 Enemies > A.7 Women with child > A.8 Fruits of the earth > A.9
Lord's Prayer > A.10 Lord's Prayer > A.11 Creed > A.12 Ten Commandments > A.13 Special
intercessions > A.14 Communicants > A.15 Blessing.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-1"></a>A.1 Exhortation / preface

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526 and Schwäbisch Hall 1543.

**Rubric.** Preface

**Bid.** To the end that all the faithful might be stirred up to pray, our Lord Christ
hath annexed unto prayer an earnest assurance, saying: Ask, and ye shall be granted; seek, and
ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-2"></a>A.2 The Church

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526, Schwäbisch Hall 1543, Frankfurt 1553, Neckarbischofsheim 1560
and Frankfurt 1589.

**Bid.** Hereupon let us diligently pray for the common Christian Church, and for the
ministers of the Church, that the Lord our God would defend them against all the assaults and
temptation of the wicked enemy, that they may abide steadfast upon the strong rock, our Lord
Christ. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, who hast revealed thy grace unto all peoples
through Jesus Christ and his Gospel: preserve, O Lord, the people of thy mercy, that thy Church
together with her ministers, scattered abroad in the whole world, may serve thee with right
faith and continue in the confession of thy name.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-3"></a>A.3 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526, Schwäbisch Hall 1543, Frankfurt 1553, Neckarbischofsheim 1560
and Frankfurt 1589.

**Bid.** Let us also pray, by the commandment and bidding of our Lord Jesus Christ and
of his apostles, for our most gracious Lord the Emperor, for all kings and officers of the
temporal government, and especially for an honourable magistracy of this city, that we may lead
a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Merciful, heavenly Father, in whose hand standeth the power and authority
of all men, set of thee for the punishment of the wicked and the welfare of the godly, in whose
hand also stand all the rights and laws of all kingdoms: we beseech thee, look graciously upon
our Lord the Emperor and all his officers, and namely upon the magistracy of this city, that
they may bear the temporal sword, committed unto them of thee, in faith, according to thy word
and commandment.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-4"></a>A.4 The afflicted

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526, Schwäbisch Hall 1543, Frankfurt 1553, Neckarbischofsheim 1560
and Frankfurt 1589.

**Bid.** Let us also pray God our Lord, that he would deliver the world from error,
and also from sicknesses, dearth, imprisonment, death, and all adversity which by the wicked
enemy is brought upon us unto our destruction. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, the comfort of the sorrowful, the strength of
the weak: let the prayer of all them that sigh unto thee in trouble and temptation come before
thy face, through our Lord Jesus Christ, that every man may feel thy help and succour in the
time of need.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-5"></a>A.5 Peace

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526, Schwäbisch Hall 1543, Frankfurt 1553, Neckarbischofsheim 1560
and Frankfurt 1589.

**Bid.** Let us also pray for a common peace and for the amendment of all Christendom,
that God would graciously endue us with temporal and everlasting peace. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, Lord of heaven and earth, by whose Spirit all
things are governed, by whose providence all things are ordered, the God of peace: we beseech
thee through our Lord Jesus Christ, that thou wouldest forgive our sins and anoint us with the
spirit of peace, that we may serve thee in fear and trembling, to the laud and praise of thy
name.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-6"></a>A.6 Enemies

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526, Schwäbisch Hall 1543 and Neckarbischofsheim 1560. *Schwäbisch
Hall 1543 lacks the rubric.*

**Rubric.** For our enemies

**Bid.** Let us also pray for our enemies, that God would lead them into the knowledge
of themselves and lead them away from their unrighteousness. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, who hast commanded us to love our enemies and
to pray for our persecutors: we cry heartily unto thee, that thou wouldest graciously visit our
enemies, and give them a friendly and one-accorded mind and heart with us and with all
Christendom.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-7"></a>A.7 Women with child

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526, Schwäbisch Hall 1543, Frankfurt 1553, Neckarbischofsheim 1560
and Frankfurt 1589.

**Bid.** Let us also pray for all women with child, that God would graciously deliver
them from the bonds of childbirth. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God and Father, Creator of all things, who hast
graciously blessed man and woman, saying: Be fruitful and multiply; and hast made the woman’s
sorrow in bearing an holy cross through our Lord Jesus Christ: we beseech thee, Lord God, that
thou wouldest preserve and keep the fruit of her womb, thine own creature, and suffer her not to
perish under the cross of the painful birth, but graciously deliver her.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-8"></a>A.8 Fruits of the earth

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526, Schwäbisch Hall 1543 and Neckarbischofsheim 1560. *Schwäbisch
Hall 1543 lacks the rubric.*

**Rubric.** For the fruits of the earth

**Bid.** Let us also pray for the fruits of the earth, that God would bless them and
let them prosper well for us. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, merciful, everlasting God, who through thy word createst and
blessest all things: we beseech thee that thou wouldest impart unto us the seed of thy word, our
Lord Jesus Christ, and sow him in our heart, whereby there may be blessed unto us, with fruitful
increase and godly use, all that serveth us for our bodily need.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-9"></a>A.9 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526 and Schwäbisch Hall 1543. *The rubric is in Schwäbisch Hall
1526 only.*

**Rubric.** Common prayer

**Bid.** Let us also pray besides for all things for which God our Lord will be prayed
unto, saying an Our Father.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-10"></a>A.10 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526.

**Rubric.** The Lord’s Prayer

**Prayer.** Our Father, which art in heaven, etc.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-11"></a>A.11 Creed

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526.

**Rubric.** The confession of the faith

**Prayer.** I believe in God the Father Almighty.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-12"></a>A.12 Ten Commandments

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526.

**Rubric.** The Ten Commandments

**Prayer.** The Lord spake all these words: I am the Lord, etc.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-13"></a>A.13 Special intercessions

*Witnesses:* Schwäbisch Hall 1526.

**Rubric.** This, then, were for the common prayer. Prayers might always be added
thereto according to matters as they befall, with wars, pestilence, or special sicknesses, etc.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-14"></a>A.14 Communicants

*Witnesses:* Frankfurt 1589.

**Prayer.** Over and above all this we beseech thee, O Lord Jesu Christ, who art the
founder and upholder of this Sacrament, that thou wouldest richly impart unto us, who appear
here to receive the same, thy Holy Spirit according to thy manifold promise, who may strengthen
and keep our hearts in undoubting faith in thy words, in true knowledge, repentance and sorrow
for our sins, and in firm trust in thy sole satisfaction for the same, that we may be partakers,
not unworthily but worthily, of the precious pledges of thy holy Body and Blood; for the honour
of thy holy sufferings and death and of this thy holy Testament. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-4-a-15"></a>A.15 Blessing

*Witnesses:* Neckarbischofsheim 1560.

**Rubric.** Appendix.

**Prayer.** Believe, and ye are heard in heaven, as the Lord hath promised us:
Whatsoever ye ask in your prayer, only believe that ye shall receive it, and it shall be done
unto you. Herewith the Lord bless you and keep you; he show you his face and have mercy upon
you, and give you his everlasting peace. Amen.

---

### <a id="s6-5"></a>6.5 Family B1: Württemberg long form

Brenz's bidding-plus-collect scheme in its ducal form: a preface on prayer (Mt 18:19, 1 Tim 2),
then biddings each followed by a collect; used chiefly on high feasts. Spread through
Pfalz-Neuburg 1554 to the Palatinate, Zweibrücken, Veldenz and Leiningen.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Württemberg 1553, long form.
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** preface, then bidding + collect for each intention.
- **Place in the service (Württemberg 1553):** On Sundays and feast days immediately after the
  sermon; the Litany is the second
  form of the common prayer.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1553 | Württemberg, Große Kirchenordnung (Brenz) | Duchy of Württemberg | Sehling 16, I/29, pp. 256–258 | bidding + collect |
| 1556 | Kurpfalz, Kirchenordnung (Ottheinrich) | Electoral Palatinate | Sehling 14, Regierungszeit Ottheinrichs, pp. 151–153 | bidding + collect |
| 1557 | Pfalz-Zweibrücken, Kirchenordnung (Pfalzgraf Wolfgang) | Palatinate-Zweibrücken (and Neuburg) | Sehling 18, I/5, pp. 193–195 | bidding + collect |
| 1566 | Leiningen-Westerburg, Kirchenordnung (Graf Philipp) | County of Leiningen-Westerburg | Sehling 19, IV/3, pp. 254–255 | preface + bidding + headed collects |
| 1574 | Pfalz-Veldenz, Kirchenordnung (Pfalzgraf Georg Johann) | Palatinate-Veldenz (Lützelstein) | Sehling 18, II/8, pp. 505–508 | bidding + collect |

Each bid ends "Bittend also:" (Pray ye thus:) and each collect "through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.",
following the family's own majority (Introduction, [Representative texts](#repo-prayers-rules), rule 4).

B1.2 to B1.4 are not one sequence but two local insertions after the preface. B1.2 is Kurpfalz
1556's lead-in to the open confession and absolution, which that order places here. B1.3 and
B1.4 are Pfalz-Veldenz 1574's own confession and absolution.

**Not in the representative text** (a minority reading of its category; see the Prayers sheet or
the critical sheets): Pfalz-Veldenz 1574 no. 9 (Peace).

**Sequence:** B1.1 Exhortation / preface > B1.2 Confession of sins > B1.3 Confession of sins >
B1.4 Confession of sins > B1.5 The Church > B1.6 Civil authority > B1.7 The afflicted > B1.8 The
erring & unbelievers > B1.9 Peace > B1.10 Enemies > B1.11 Women with child > B1.12 Fruits of the
earth > B1.13 Lord's Prayer.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-1"></a>B1.1 Exhortation / preface

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574.

**Rubric.** The preface of the common prayer.

**Bid.** Forasmuch as we are gathered together in God’s name, and it is commanded us
that we should call upon God in all our need and also make our intercession for every man,
whereunto we have the promise of our dear Lord Christ: Where two of you shall agree on earth as
touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in
heaven; and: Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be
opened unto you.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-2"></a>B1.2 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1556.

**Bid.** Hereupon, forasmuch as we neither can nor may come before the throne of the
divine majesty in our prayer with a comforted conscience and sure faith, except we be first
reconciled with God and received of him into grace; and we come by no other way unto
reconciliation with God, but that we acknowledge our sins and believe that our sins are forgiven
and remitted us for the sake of the only-begotten Son of God, our dear Lord Jesus Christ: let us
therefore first confess our sins before God and thereafter receive the absolution from our sins,
saying thus: I, poor sinner, etc., as above.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-3"></a>B1.3 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Pfalz-Veldenz 1574.

**Rubric.** Confession and acknowledgement.

**Bid.** That our prayer be not despised and cast away of God, as flowing out of an
unclean, impenitent heart, we will first of all confess our sins and misdeeds unto the Almighty
with true repentance and sorrow, and in the name of his beloved Son Jesus Christ pray for pardon
out of true faith. Therefore lift up your hearts and say with me this open confession:

**Prayer.** I, a poor, wretched, sinful man, confess before God, my Creator and
Redeemer, that I, alas, have oft and many times sinned right grievously, not only with gross
outward words and works, but much more with inward, inborn blindness, weakness, doubting,
impatience, hatred and envy, covetousness, pride and haughtiness, and with other evil wiles,
which my heavenly Father well knoweth in me, and which I, alas, cannot so perfectly know. But
they repent me from my heart and grieve me; I desire also from my heart grace and pardon of God,
for the sake of his beloved Son, our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, who hath shed his innocent
blood for the sins of the whole world.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-4"></a>B1.4 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Pfalz-Veldenz 1574.

**Rubric.** Absolution.

**Prayer.** The almighty, merciful God hath had mercy upon us, and forgiveth us truly
all our sins for the sake of his dear Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, whom he gave into death for
our sakes, and hath given power to become the children of God to all that believe on his name;
he giveth us moreover his Holy Spirit, that we may believe and be saved. This grant us God,
Father, Son and Holy Ghost. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-5"></a>B1.5 The Church

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574.

**Bid.** Hereupon let us, out of true confidence in the divine mercy, through our Lord
Jesus Christ, pray for the common Christian Church and the ministers thereof. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** O almighty, gracious God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath
first commanded us that we should pray thee for labourers into thine harvest: we beseech thy
bottomless mercy that thou wouldest send us right and true teachers and ministers of thy divine
word, and give thy wholesome word into their heart and mouth, that they may faithfully perform
thy commandment and preach nothing that is contrary to thy holy word; to the end that we, being
by thy heavenly, eternal word admonished, taught, fed, comforted and strengthened, may do that
which is well-pleasing unto thee and profitable unto us. Give, O Lord, unto thy holy Christendom
thy Spirit and divine wisdom, that thy word may run and grow among us and be preached with all
boldness, as it becometh, and that thy holy Christian congregation may be bettered thereby; that
we may serve thee with steadfast faith and continue in the knowledge of thy name unto the end.
Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-6"></a>B1.6 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574. *Leiningen-Westerburg 1566 lacks the bid.*

**Rubric.** For the temporal magistrates.

**Bid.** Let us faithfully pray, by the commandment of our Lord Jesus Christ and of
his Apostles, for all temporal magistrates, that we may lead a quiet and still life in all
godliness. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, in whose hand standeth all power and authority
of men, ordained of thee for the punishment of the wicked and the welfare of the godly, in whose
hand also stand all the rights and laws of all realms upon earth: we beseech thee, look
graciously upon thy servants, the Roman Emperor, all kings, princes and lawful magistrates, and
especially upon our gracious prince and lord of this land, and also all his counsellors and
officers, that they may bear the temporal sword, committed unto them of thee, according to thy
commandment in thy fear. Enlighten them and keep them in thy divine name; give them, dear Lord,
wisdom and understanding and a peaceable government, that they may defend and rule all their
subjects in peace, rest and unity; and prolong their days, O God of our salvation, that under
their dominion we together with them may hallow and praise thy divine name; through our Lord
Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-7"></a>B1.7 The afflicted

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574. *Leiningen-Westerburg 1566 lacks the bid.*

**Rubric.** For all manner of trouble and temptation.

**Bid.** Let us pray for all them that are in trouble and temptation by reason of
sickness, dearth, war, imprisonment, pestilence, and are burdened and laden with all manner of
adversity, that God would graciously show them help and succour in their need. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** O almighty Lord God, who despisest not the sighing of the wretched, and
settest not at nought the desire of the sorrowful hearts: look thou upon our prayer, which we
bring before thee in our need, and hear us graciously, that all that striveth against us, both
from the devil and from men, may be brought to nought and by the grace of thy goodness be
scattered; that we, being hurt by no temptation, may give thanks unto thee in thy congregation
and praise thee evermore; through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-8"></a>B1.8 The erring & unbelievers

*Witnesses:* Pfalz-Veldenz 1574.

**Rubric.** For them that are in error of the faith, that God would graciously convert
them, etc.

**Prayer.** Lord God, heavenly Father, who willest that all men come to the knowledge
of thee and be saved: we pray thee earnestly and with our whole heart that thou wouldest visit
in fatherly wise all them that are fallen away from the Christian faith, or else are erring in
certain articles and are possessed and led astray with false doctrine, and bring them again to
the knowledge of their error, that they may win delight and pleasure in thy steadfast, simple,
eternal truth; through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-9"></a>B1.9 Peace

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574. *Leiningen-Westerburg 1566 lacks the bid.*

**Rubric.** For the common peace.

**Bid.** Let us also pray right earnestly for a common peace in the land, that the
true service of God may grow up among us and Christian discipline increase. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, a King of glory and a Lord of heaven and of
earth, by whose Spirit all things are governed, by whose providence all things are ordered; who
art a God of peace, from whom alone all unity cometh unto us: we beseech thee through our Lord
Jesus Christ that thou wouldest forgive us our sins and endue us with thy divine peace and
unity, that we may serve thee in fear and trembling, to the laud and praise of thy name. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-10"></a>B1.10 Enemies

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574. *Leiningen-Westerburg 1566 and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574 lack the bid.*

**Rubric.** For the enemies.

**Bid.** Let us also pray for our enemies, that God would remember them with grace and
graciously vouchsafe them that which is profitable and needful to their salvation. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, who hast commanded us that we should love our
enemies, do good to them that hurt us, and pray for our persecutors: we cry earnestly unto thee
that thou wouldest graciously visit all our enemies, vouchsafe them true repentance of their
sins, and give them, together with us and the whole of Christendom, a friendly, God-fearing, and
single mind and heart; through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-11"></a>B1.11 Women with child

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574. *Leiningen-Westerburg 1566 and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574 lack the bid.*

**Rubric.** For all women with child.

**Bid.** Let us also pray for all women with child, that God would graciously deliver
them from the bonds of childbirth. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God and Father, a Creator of all things, who hast
graciously blessed man and woman, and hast blessed unto the woman her pains in bearing to be an
holy cross: we beseech thee, gracious Father, that thou wouldest keep and preserve the fruits of
their womb, and not let it perish under the cross in the sorrowful travail, but graciously and
with joy make them to feel thy help; through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-12"></a>B1.12 Fruits of the earth

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Leiningen-Westerburg 1566
and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574. *Leiningen-Westerburg 1566 lacks the bid.*

**Rubric.** For the fruits of the earth.

**Bid.** Let us also pray for the fruits of the earth, that God would bless them and
graciously vouchsafe them unto us, to enjoy the same in obedience unto him. Pray ye thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, who by thy word createst and blessest all
things: we beseech thee that thou wouldest plant thy Word, our Lord Jesus Christ, in our heart,
whereby all that serveth us for our bodily need may be blessed unto us with fruitful increase
and godly use; through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-5-b1-13"></a>B1.13 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557 and Pfalz-Veldenz 1574.

**Bid.** Let us also pray for all that for which our Lord God will be prayed, saying:
Our Father, etc.

### <a id="s6-6"></a>6.6 Family B2: Württemberg short form

The same intentions compressed into a single continuous prayer ("Almighty, eternal God, heavenly Father …") after a brief exhortation; the ordinary Sunday form. The most widely
copied general prayer in the corpus, reaching Saxony (1580), Magdeburg, Strasbourg, Sayn, Nassau
and the Ysenburg counties.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Württemberg 1553, short form.
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** exhortation + one continuous prayer.
- **Place in the service (Württemberg 1553):** After the sermon, when time does not allow the
  long form to be read.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1553 | Württemberg, Große Kirchenordnung (Brenz) | Duchy of Württemberg | Sehling 16, I/29, pp. 261–262 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1556 | Kurpfalz, Kirchenordnung (Ottheinrich) | Electoral Palatinate | Sehling 14, Regierungszeit Ottheinrichs, pp. 157–159 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1557 | Pfalz-Zweibrücken, Kirchenordnung (Pfalzgraf Wolfgang) | Palatinate-Zweibrücken (and Neuburg) | Sehling 18, I/5, pp. 195–196 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1559 | Rothenburg ob der Tauber, Kirchenordnung | Rothenburg ob der Tauber (Imperial city) | Sehling 11, VI.1, pp. 587–588 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1562 | Erzstift Magdeburg, Visitationsordnung 1562 (Administrator Sigismund of Brandenburg) | Archbishopric of Magdeburg | Sehling 2, Erzbisthum Magdeburg Nr. 1, p. 420 | prescription of contents (indirect speech) |
| 1574 | Pfalz-Veldenz, Kirchenordnung (Pfalzgraf Georg Johann) | Palatinate-Veldenz (Lützelstein) | Sehling 18, II/8, pp. 508–509 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1578 | Hohenlohe, Kirchenordnung | County of Hohenlohe | Sehling 15, Nr. 25, pp. 263–264 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1579 | Nördlingen, Kirchenordnung | Nördlingen (Imperial city) | Sehling 12, VIII.7, pp. 367–368 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1580 | Kursachsen, Kirchenordnung (Kurfürst August) | Electorate of Saxony | Sehling 1, II. Theil, Nr. 40, pp. 370–371 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1582 | Ysenburg-Ronneburg, Agende | County of Ysenburg-Ronneburg | Sehling 10, III/Ysenburg-Ronneburg Nr. 3, pp. 575–576 | confession + continuous prayer |
| 1588 | Ysenburg-Birstein, Kirchenordnung | County of Ysenburg-Büdingen-Birstein | Sehling 10, III/Ysenburg-Birstein Nr. 14, pp. 621–622 | exhortation + confession + continuous prayer |
| 1590 | Sayn, Kirchenordnung 1590 (Graf Heinrich IV.) | County of Sayn | Sehling 19, V/18, pp. 408–410 | preface + continuous prayer |
| 1598 | Straßburg, Kirchenordnung (9 April 1598) | Strasbourg (Imperial city) | Sehling 20/1, Nr. 61, pp. 588–589 | exhortation + continuous prayer |
| 1603 | Wild- und Rheingrafschaft, Kirchenordnung [nach 1603] | Wild- and Rhinegraviate (Salm-Kyrburg, Dhaun, Grumbach) | Sehling 19, VII/21, pp. 622–623 | exhortation + confession + absolution + continuous prayer + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1605 | Pfalz-Veldenz, Kirchenordnung Lützelstein | Palatinate-Veldenz (Lützelstein) | Sehling 18, II/11, pp. 585–586 | continuous prayer |
| 1618 | Nassau-Weilburg (Nassau-Saarbrücken), Kirchenordnung und Agende 1617/1618 | Counties of Nassau-Weilburg and Saarbrücken | Sehling 10, I/Nassau-Weilburg Nr. 1 (appendix: KO 1617, Agende 1618), p. 314 | continuous prayer |
| 1618 | Rothenberg, Vereinigung, wie es mit den kirchenactibus soll gehalten werden | Ganerbschaft Rothenberg (Franconia) | Sehling 13, V.1–2, pp. 548–549 | continuous prayer |

Magdeburg 1562 prescribes the contents of the prayer in indirect speech ("that he also [would grant] to the temporal magistrates …"). Where no other witness has a bid, its sentences fill the bid column.
B2.2 is its opening, and the bids of B2.6 and B2.9 are its words. They are paraphrases of the
prayer, not words said to the people.

The confession and absolution (B2.3, B2.4) are those of the Ysenburg orders of 1582 and 1588 and
the Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603. B2.12, B2.13 and B2.15 each come from a single witness
(Rothenberg 1618, Rothenburg 1559, Nördlingen 1579) and stand where that order has them.

**Not in the representative text** (a minority reading of its category; see the Prayers sheet or
the critical sheets): Hohenlohe 1578 no. 1 (Exhortation / preface); Nördlingen 1579 no. 1
(Exhortation / preface); Ysenburg-Birstein 1588 no. 1 (Exhortation / preface); Sayn 1590 no. 1
(Exhortation / preface); Strassburg 1598 no. 1 (Exhortation / preface); Strassburg 1598 no. 8
(Special intercessions); Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603 no. 1 (Exhortation / preface); Wild- und
Rheingrafschaft 1603 no. 3 (Confession of sins); Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603 no. 10 (Lord's
Prayer); Lützelstein 1605 no. 1 (Special intercessions).

**Sequence:** B2.1 Exhortation / preface > B2.2 Thanksgiving > B2.3 Confession of sins > B2.4
Confession of sins > B2.5 The Church > B2.6 Civil authority > B2.7 Enemies > B2.8 The erring &
unbelievers > B2.9 The afflicted > B2.10 Fruits of the earth > B2.11 Conclusion > B2.12
Communicants > B2.13 Lord's Prayer > B2.14 Lord's Prayer > B2.15 Special intercessions.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-1"></a>B2.1 Exhortation / preface

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Rothenburg 1559,
Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Nördlingen 1579 and Kursachsen 1580.

**Rubric.** A shorter form of the common prayer. But forasmuch as it cometh to pass at
times that the prayers cannot well be rehearsed at length, then may the following prayer,
wherein all the concerns of the Church are briefly comprehended, be said after the sermon:

**Bid.** Dearly beloved in Christ, forasmuch as we are all members of one body,
whereof Christ is the head, so ought one member to take the part of another and to pray one for
another; and this we should do gladly from the heart, by the commandment of our Lord Christ and
of his holy Apostle. Pray ye thus:

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-2"></a>B2.2 Thanksgiving

*Witnesses:* Magdeburg 1562.

**Rubric.** How they hold the common prayer. (In the margin: Reminder concerning the
common prayer.)

**Bid.** And the ministers of the Church in the villages and in the small towns here
shall be reminded by our visitors that in the common prayer, which is always made after the
sermon, they give thanks unto the merciful God for the revelation and preservation of his divine
word,

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-3"></a>B2.3 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582, Ysenburg-Birstein 1588 and Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603.
*The bid is in Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582 only.*

**Bid.** Confess with me your sins before God; say from the heart:

**Prayer.** Lord God, heavenly Father, I, a poor sinful man, confess before thee that
I, alas, have sinned grievously and much against thee with words, works, thoughts, doing and
leaving undone, as thou, O God, knowest it in me, and I, alas, cannot confess it. It repenteth
me and grieveth me from my heart. I desire grace and forgiveness of my sins through Jesus Christ
thy dear Son.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-4"></a>B2.4 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582 and Ysenburg-Birstein 1588.

**Prayer.** To all them that are heartily sorry for their sins, fear and are
affrighted before God’s wrath, but desire grace and believe on Jesus Christ, and purpose to
amend their life, unto them I declare by the commandment of God that God will have mercy upon
them, pardon their sins, and give them eternal life for the sake of Jesus Christ his dear Son.
But they that acknowledge not their sins, fear not God’s wrath, but continue and go on in sins
with impenitence, and believe not on Jesus Christ, but trust in their own works and worthiness
or in aught else apart from Christ: upon them the wrath of God abideth until the time of their
amendment.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-5"></a>B2.5 The Church

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Rothenburg 1559, Magdeburg
1562, Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Hohenlohe 1578, Nördlingen 1579, Kursachsen 1580, Ysenburg-Ronneburg
1582, Ysenburg-Birstein 1588, Sayn 1590, Strassburg 1598, Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603,
Lützelstein 1605, Nassau-Weilburg 1618 and Rothenberg 1618. *The bid is in Magdeburg 1562,
Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582, Ysenburg-Birstein 1588 and Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603 only.*
*Magdeburg 1562 lacks the prayer.*

**Bid.** Let us pray:

**Prayer.** Almighty, merciful, everlasting God and Father, a Lord of heaven and of
earth: we beseech thee heartily that thou wouldest govern thy holy Church with her ministers by
the Holy Ghost, that they may be kept in the right and true pasture of thine almighty and
everlasting word, whereby faith toward thee may be strengthened, and love toward all men may
spring up and increase in us.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-6"></a>B2.6 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Rothenburg 1559, Magdeburg
1562, Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Hohenlohe 1578, Nördlingen 1579, Kursachsen 1580, Ysenburg-Ronneburg
1582, Ysenburg-Birstein 1588, Sayn 1590, Strassburg 1598, Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603,
Lützelstein 1605, Nassau-Weilburg 1618 and Rothenberg 1618. *The bid is in Magdeburg 1562 only.*
*Magdeburg 1562 lacks the prayer.*

**Bid.** that he would also vouchsafe unto the temporal magistrates, the Roman
Emperor, all Christian kings, Electors, princes and lords, but especially unto us as prince of
the land, our kind and dearly beloved consort, the young lordship and damsels, and also the
whole most laudable Electoral and princely house of Brandenburg, long life, abiding health and
prosperous government, together with all temporal and eternal welfare; and likewise unto all our
counsellors and officers understanding, grace and unity to rule the subjects according to his
divine will and good pleasure, that righteousness may be furthered and wickedness hindered and
punished, that we may accomplish our life in quiet rest and good peace, as becometh Christians;

**Prayer.** Vouchsafe also unto the temporal magistrates, the Roman Emperor, all
kings, princes and lords, but especially unto our gracious lord and prince of this land, and
also the whole house of Württemberg, together with all their counsellors and officers, grace and
unity to rule the subjects according to thy divine will and good pleasure; that righteousness
may be furthered, and wickedness hindered and punished, that we may accomplish our life in quiet
rest and good peace, as becometh Christians.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-7"></a>B2.7 Enemies

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Rothenburg 1559,
Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Hohenlohe 1578, Nördlingen 1579, Kursachsen 1580, Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582,
Ysenburg-Birstein 1588, Sayn 1590, Strassburg 1598, Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603, Lützelstein
1605, Nassau-Weilburg 1618 and Rothenberg 1618.

**Prayer.** That our enemies and adversaries also may desist, and yield themselves to
live with us peaceably and gently.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-8"></a>B2.8 The erring & unbelievers

*Witnesses:* Pfalz-Veldenz 1574 and Lützelstein 1605.

**Prayer.** And all that err, are led astray, and are apostate, wilt thou, O gracious
God, bring to the truth of thy word and the knowledge of thy holy name.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-9"></a>B2.9 The afflicted

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Rothenburg 1559, Magdeburg
1562, Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Hohenlohe 1578, Nördlingen 1579, Kursachsen 1580, Ysenburg-Ronneburg
1582, Ysenburg-Birstein 1588, Sayn 1590, Strassburg 1598, Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603,
Lützelstein 1605, Nassau-Weilburg 1618 and Rothenberg 1618. *The bid is in Magdeburg 1562 only.*
*Magdeburg 1562 lacks the prayer.*

**Bid.** and, as the form of the common prayer is further wont to go, for the fruits
of the earth, for all the sorrowful, poor and sick that are assailed by the devil or by men, for
them that for his holy name’s sake and for the truth’s sake are taken captive or otherwise
suffer persecution, and whatsoever more there be of like tribulation and burden.

**Prayer.** All them that are in tribulation, poverty, sickness, the bonds of
childbirth, and other temptation, and them also that for thy holy name’s sake and for the
truth’s sake are assailed, taken captive, or otherwise suffer persecution: comfort them, O God,
with thy Holy Spirit, that they may receive and acknowledge all this as thy fatherly will.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-10"></a>B2.10 Fruits of the earth

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Rothenburg 1559,
Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Hohenlohe 1578, Nördlingen 1579, Kursachsen 1580, Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582,
Ysenburg-Birstein 1588, Sayn 1590, Strassburg 1598, Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603, Lützelstein
1605, Nassau-Weilburg 1618 and Rothenberg 1618.

**Prayer.** Cause also all the fruits of the earth that pertain to our bodily need to
prosper and thrive for us with fruitful increase.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-11"></a>B2.11 Conclusion

*Witnesses:* Württemberg 1553, Kurpfalz 1556, Pfalz-Zweibrücken 1557, Rothenburg 1559,
Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Hohenlohe 1578, Nördlingen 1579, Kursachsen 1580, Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582,
Ysenburg-Birstein 1588, Sayn 1590, Strassburg 1598, Wild- und Rheingrafschaft 1603, Lützelstein
1605, Nassau-Weilburg 1618 and Rothenberg 1618.

**Prayer.** We pray also for all that for which thou, everlasting God, wilt be prayed,
that thou wouldest graciously vouchsafe us the same, through the bitter suffering and death of
Christ Jesus, thine only Son, our beloved Lord and Saviour, who with thee and the Holy Ghost
liveth and reigneth, equal God, highly praised, for ever. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-12"></a>B2.12 Communicants

*Witnesses:* Rothenberg 1618.

**Rubric.** Note. When there are communicants, one shall not omit to pray for them
also, that they may receive the holy Supper unto life in true knowledge and repentance of their
sins, in saving faith in Christ, and in a Christian purpose to amend their life.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-13"></a>B2.13 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Rothenburg 1559.

**Rubric.** And let every one say an Our Father thereupon.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-14"></a>B2.14 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Pfalz-Veldenz 1574, Hohenlohe 1578, Ysenburg-Ronneburg 1582, Ysenburg-Birstein
1588, Lützelstein 1605 and Nassau-Weilburg 1618. *Hohenlohe 1578 lacks the prayer.*

**Prayer.** Our Father, etc.

#### <a id="s6-6-b2-15"></a>B2.15 Special intercessions

*Witnesses:* Nördlingen 1579.

**Rubric.** Thereupon the special needs that befall, as the sick, the publishing of
the married folk, feast days, etc., are to be announced, and it is to be concluded with the Our
Father, together with the blessing:

**Prayer.** The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion
of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen.

---

### <a id="s6-7"></a>6.7 Family C: Bidding exhortation (Strasbourg type)

A bidding exhortation in the Strasbourg manner: the minister tells the people what to pray for,
item by item, without addressing God, and ends with the Our Father.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Hanau-Lichtenberg 1573.
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** bidding exhortation + Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Hanau-Lichtenberg 1573):** After the sermon; then a psalm is sung by
  school and congregation, followed by a collect and the blessing. The pastor is to refer to the
  sermon just preached and to present needs (war, plague, dearth) in the common prayer.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1573 | Hanau-Lichtenberg, Kirchenordnung (Graf Philipp IV.) | County of Hanau-Lichtenberg (Alsace) | Sehling 20/2, Hanau-Lichtenberg Nr. 6, pp. 52–53 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |

**Sequence:** C.1 Exhortation / preface > C.2 The Word & its fruit > C.3 Civil authority > C.4
All estates / households > C.5 Fruits of the earth > C.6 The afflicted > C.7 Special
intercessions > C.8 Lord's Prayer.

#### <a id="s6-7-c-1"></a>C.1 Exhortation / preface

**Rubric.** After the sermon let the common prayer be made on this wise:

**Bid.** Dear friends, forasmuch as we are gathered together and have heard God’s
word, we will lay all the need of the whole of Christendom before our Lord God, and pray him
that he would be gracious and merciful unto us, and give all that is profitable and needful for
us, for the necessity of the body and for the salvation of the soul:

#### <a id="s6-7-c-2"></a>C.2 The Word & its fruit

**Bid.** First, pray ye for the spiritual estate: that our dear Lord God would let his
holy word be preached unto us, and vouchsafe grace that we may gladly hear the same, believe it
with the heart, and order our life thereafter; and that he would comfort, strengthen, and
deliver out of all misery and woe all those that for the sake of this Word are in misery, woe
and adversity. That he would also graciously enlighten by his Word and Holy Spirit all that are
yet in darkness, error and idolatry, and bring them to the knowledge of the truth, that they
with us and we with them may be saved.

#### <a id="s6-7-c-3"></a>C.3 Civil authority

**Bid.** Secondly, pray ye for the temporal government: first for the head, his Roman
Imperial Majesty, our most gracious lord; then for the members, as the Electors, princes and
lords of all Christendom; but especially for our gracious lords, lady and damsels of Hanau, for
their Graces’ counsellors, officers, servants and the whole lordship, for a worshipful court and
commune here, and also the neighbourhood round about. Almighty God vouchsafe unto the
magistrates his Holy Spirit and wisdom, that they may rule in Christian wise and well, and keep
and preserve the subjects in common peace.

#### <a id="s6-7-c-4"></a>C.4 All estates / households

**Bid.** Lastly, pray ye also for the estate of matrimony: Almighty God vouchsafe unto
all married folk his Holy Spirit, that they may live together in Christian wise, peaceably and
in concord, and may bring up their children and household in the fear of God, and also in honour
and virtue.

#### <a id="s6-7-c-5"></a>C.5 Fruits of the earth

**Bid.** Pray ye for the fruit of the field, for seasonable weather, and for all that
is needful unto us.

#### <a id="s6-7-c-6"></a>C.6 The afflicted

**Bid.** May our Lord God tend and keep children and the sick, give unto women with
child and them that give suck joyful fruit and increase, and loose and set free the captives.

#### <a id="s6-7-c-7"></a>C.7 Special intercessions

**Bid.** And let every man consider his own need and come with it before God, the
heavenly Father, and doubt not that he will graciously hear us through Christ. And say with your
whole heart thus:

#### <a id="s6-7-c-8"></a>C.8 Lord's Prayer

**Prayer.** Our Father, which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come.
Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us
our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil:
For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen.

---

### <a id="s6-8"></a>6.8 Family D: Nürnberg-type Vermahnung zum Gebet

"Vermahnung zum Gebet" (Exhortation to prayer): an exhortation in the second person ("Dear friends, pray …") listing
the intentions, closed by the Our Father. Copied in Waldeck, Erbach, Solms-Laubach and
Henneberg.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Nürnberg 1545 (Veit Dietrich).
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** bidding exhortation + Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Nürnberg 1545):** In the “Order of the Mass in the country, where there are no schools”: after the opening German psalm the pastor reads, in place of the Epistle, this
  exhortation with the Our Father, followed by the Creed, the Ten Commandments and the catechism
  pieces on Baptism, the Keys and the Supper (the medieval pulpit office, Prone).

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1545 | Nürnberg, Agendbüchlein für die Pfarrherren auf dem Land (Veit Dietrich) | Nürnberg (Imperial city) and its rural parishes | Sehling 11, V.1, pp. 500–501 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1556 | Waldeck, Kirchenordnung (Kirchen Ordnung auff den Dörffern) | County of Waldeck | Sehling 9, II/Waldeck Nr. 15 (Kirchenordnung 1556), pp. 273–274 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1560 | Erbach, Kirchenordnung (Graf Georg) | County of Erbach | Sehling 9, IV/Erbach Nr. 6 (2. Erbacher Kirchenordnung 1560), pp. 428–429 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1576 | Solms-Laubach, Kirchenordnung [1576–1580] | County of Solms-Laubach | Sehling 9, III/Solms Nr. 10, pp. 360–361 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1582 | Henneberg, Kirchenordnung (Graf Georg Ernst) | County of Henneberg | Sehling 2, Henneberg Nr. 3, p. 308 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |

The family has two lines, and the representative text joins them. Veit Dietrich's exhortation
(Nürnberg 1545, copied in Waldeck 1556) supplies D.3, D.7, D.12 and D.14. The Erbach line
(Erbach 1560, Solms-Laubach 1576, Henneberg 1582) supplies most of the rest, and it has the
majority for the magistrates (D.6). So the text has two openings: D.3 (Nürnberg) and D.4
(Erbach). To read Veit Dietrich's prayer alone, use the Prayers sheet of the workbook, or the
critical sheets.

**Not in the representative text** (a minority reading of its category; see the Prayers sheet or
the critical sheets): Nürnberg 1545 no. 2 (Civil authority); Waldeck 1556 no. 2 (Civil
authority); Erbach 1560 no. 7 (All estates / households); Erbach 1560 no. 8 (Lord's Prayer);
Solms-Laubach 1576 no. 5 (All estates / households); Solms-Laubach 1576 no. 7 (Special
intercessions); Henneberg 1582 no. 5 (All estates / households); Henneberg 1582 no. 9 (Special
intercessions).

**Sequence:** D.1 Exhortation / preface > D.2 Thanksgiving > D.3 The Word & its fruit > D.4 The
Church > D.5 Peace > D.6 Civil authority > D.7 All estates / households > D.8 The persecuted >
D.9 The afflicted > D.10 The erring & unbelievers > D.11 Women with child > D.12 Lord's Prayer >
D.13 Special intercessions > D.14 Creed > D.15 Blessing.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-1"></a>D.1 Exhortation / preface

*Witnesses:* Henneberg 1582.

**Rubric.** After the sermon the minister shall again diligently exhort the people to
prayer for all estates and the need of the Christian Church by means of the following form. ¶
Form of the common prayer.

**Bid.** Beloved in the Lord Christ, forasmuch as we are now here gathered together in
the name of our Lord Christ, and have God’s commandment and bidding that we should pray, and
moreover the promise that whatsoever we ask in the name of Jesus Christ, our gracious Father in
heaven will gladly give it us:

#### <a id="s6-8-d-2"></a>D.2 Thanksgiving

*Witnesses:* Solms-Laubach 1576.

**Rubric.** At the end of the sermon the matters handled shall be briefly repeated,
and then, if there be persons that have given in their names as betrothed one to another, they
shall be proclaimed; whereupon thanksgiving and prayer shall follow, thus: ¶ Thanksgiving and
common prayer

**Bid.** Forasmuch now as we have heard God’s word, and are bound to give thanks unto
God Almighty for all his benefits which he daily showeth us, we will give him thanks for the
work of creation, redemption and sanctification; that he still keepeth us evermore in his
knowledge until the last day, and vouchsafeth his grace to the spiritual, temporal and household
estate, and blesseth us. We are bound also to pray for the preservation of the same estates and
what pertaineth thereto; and we have God’s promise and sure assurance that whatsoever we shall
ask in the name of Jesus Christ, the Father in heaven will give it us.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-3"></a>D.3 The Word & its fruit

*Witnesses:* Nürnberg 1545 and Waldeck 1556.

**Rubric.** Exhortation to pray for all manner of estates:

**Bid.** Ye elect, pray God the Father of all mercy, through Jesus Christ our dear
Lord, for the fruitful increase of the holy Gospel, that he would send right and true labourers
into his harvest, and graciously enlighten both ministers and hearers of the word, to the
hallowing of his blessed name, the increase of his kingdom and the fulfilling of his divine
will.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-4"></a>D.4 The Church

*Witnesses:* Erbach 1560, Solms-Laubach 1576 and Henneberg 1582.

**Bid.** Let us therefore first consider the need of all Christendom, and pray that
God would keep his word pure and clear unto us, and also bring thereto them that are not yet
come to the right knowledge, and graciously guard his poor Christendom against all the devices
of the devil.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-5"></a>D.5 Peace

*Witnesses:* Erbach 1560, Solms-Laubach 1576 and Henneberg 1582.

**Bid.** Thereafter let us also pray for this temporal life, that God would bless us
with gracious peace and seasonable weather, and keep us from dearth, war and pestilence.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-6"></a>D.6 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Erbach 1560, Solms-Laubach 1576 and Henneberg 1582.

**Bid.** Pray ye also for all magistrates, Emperor, kings, princes and lords,
especially for our gracious lordship here, that God would enlighten their hearts by his Spirit
and word, that God’s word and honour may be furthered and not hindered by them, and that we also
may have the more peace under their government.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-7"></a>D.7 All estates / households

*Witnesses:* Nürnberg 1545 and Waldeck 1556.

**Bid.** Further, pray ye for all married folk, masters and mistresses of households,
labourers, tradesmen, servants, sinners men and women, the sick, the captives, the sorrowful,
forsaken widows and orphans, and them that are in temptation, sorrowful, erring and misled
consciences, or whatsoever else there be of the like. The eternal, gracious God have mercy upon
all, pardon their misdeeds, vouchsafe them an honourable, peaceable, honest conversation
according to his word, and let them sink in no temptation, but graciously deliver them from all
evil, be it bodily or ghostly, through pure doctrine and firm faith. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-8"></a>D.8 The persecuted

*Witnesses:* Erbach 1560 and Henneberg 1582.

**Bid.** Forasmuch also as here and there in all lands many poor Christians are for
the word of God and for righteousness’ sake persecuted, driven out, cast into prison, miserably
tormented and slain, we are bound to pray God for them, that he would comfort and strengthen
their hearts by his Holy Spirit, keep them steadfast in the confession, and help them blessedly
in body and soul.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-9"></a>D.9 The afflicted

*Witnesses:* Erbach 1560, Solms-Laubach 1576 and Henneberg 1582.

**Bid.** Thereafter let us also pray for our poor brethren and sisters, here and in
the whole world, where there is either grievous sickness or great temptation, that God would
graciously deliver them.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-10"></a>D.10 The erring & unbelievers

*Witnesses:* Henneberg 1582.

**Bid.** Lastly pray ye also for the poor people that yet lie under the papacy in
error and an evil conscience, and have not the blessed knowledge of the word as we have, that
God would lead them also to such light of his grace and make them with us eternally blessed
through right faith in Christ.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-11"></a>D.11 Women with child

*Witnesses:* Erbach 1560.

**Bid.** Pray ye also for all women with child, that they may be graciously delivered
from the bonds of childbirth; for these and all other necessities of the whole of Christendom;
and also for our enemies, that they may be converted and brought to the right knowledge of our
Lord Jesus Christ.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-12"></a>D.12 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Nürnberg 1545, Waldeck 1556, Solms-Laubach 1576 and Henneberg 1582. *Solms-Laubach
1576 lacks the bid.* *The prayer is in Nürnberg 1545 and Solms-Laubach 1576 only.*
