**Bid.** To obtain all this, say out of right faith:

**Prayer.** Our Father …, but deliver us from evil: for thine is the kingdom, and the
power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-13"></a>D.13 Special intercessions

*Witnesses:* Erbach 1560.

**Rubric.** So also at any time, by reason of need befalling, as in wars, pestilence
and dearth, special prayers serving thereto may for that time be added and used.

#### <a id="s6-8-d-14"></a>D.14 Creed

*Witnesses:* Nürnberg 1545.

**Rubric.** The articles of our faith.

**Prayer.** I believe in God the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, …

#### <a id="s6-8-d-15"></a>D.15 Blessing

*Witnesses:* Henneberg 1582.

**Rubric.** After such exhortation and the Our Father said, the preacher shall speak
the following blessing over the people:

**Prayer.** The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, and the communion of
the Holy Ghost be with you all. Amen.

---

### <a id="s6-9"></a>6.9 Family E: Saxon Gemein Gebet (Melanchthon/Pfeffinger)

The Albertine Saxon "Gemein Gebet" (Common prayer) in the Melanchthon/Pfeffinger tradition, a continuous prayer
with pronounced petitions against war and for the Elector.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Leipzig 1567.
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** continuous prayer.
- **Place in the service (Leipzig 1567):** After the sermon, “to be said with mouth and heart”.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1567 | Leipzig, Gemein gebet (renewed by Johann Pfeffinger) | Leipzig (Electoral Saxony) | Sehling 1, IV. Theil, Nr. 108, pp. 595–596 | continuous prayer |

**Sequence:** E.1 Repentance & forgiveness > E.2 The Church > E.3 Civil authority > E.4 Peace >
E.5 Civil authority > E.6 The afflicted.

#### <a id="s6-9-e-1"></a>E.1 Repentance & forgiveness

**Rubric.** Common prayer. To be said after the sermon with mouth and heart.

**Prayer.** Almighty God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, we confess that we are
defiled with many sins, wittingly and unwittingly, and it grieveth us heartily that we have done
against thy righteous will; and we beseech thee that thou wouldest turn our hearts unto thee,
and forgive us all our sins for thy dear Son Jesus Christ’s sake, and kindle in us by thy Holy
Spirit right faith and right obedience, and govern us. So is it also our earnest purpose to
amend ourselves with thy help and to live in thy obedience.

#### <a id="s6-9-e-2"></a>E.2 The Church

**Prayer.** We beseech thee also, for thy dear Son Jesus Christ’s sake, that thou
wouldest evermore gather a Church among us in these lands, and preserve Christian pure doctrine,
and give faithful teachers and preachers, which with right doctrine and good example may serve
to thy praise and the salvation of the people.

#### <a id="s6-9-e-3"></a>E.3 Civil authority

**Prayer.** And we beseech thee from our heart that thou wouldest, for thy dear Son
Jesus Christ’s sake, give unto these lands peaceable, Christian, blessed government, and govern
with the Holy Spirit the Roman Imperial Majesty and our lordships, the duke regent Elector and
his Electoral Grace’s adherents and kinsfolk, that their life and government may serve to thy
praise, and to peace and salvation for them and for the subjects.

#### <a id="s6-9-e-4"></a>E.4 Peace

**Prayer.** Wilt thou also by thy bottomless mercy guard, protect and preserve his
Electoral Grace, together with his adherents and kinsmen, in these grievous and other matters of
war; graciously convert the adversaries, the unquiet and disobedient, which resist the divine
ordinance, despise authority, break the peace, and give occasion to bloodshed and the ruin of
people and land, or else restrain and withstand them; and bring the lawful war committed unto us
to a good, happy, peaceable end with blessed welfare, that the innocent bloodshed of many
Christians and the wasting of these lands, schools and churches may be turned away and
prevented.

#### <a id="s6-9-e-5"></a>E.5 Civil authority

**Prayer.** And wilt thou also graciously govern and preserve the magistrates and
subjects of this city, and willingly give and bless the fruits of the earth (which thou givest
that men may be preserved in this bodily life, to learn to know thee and call upon thee) and our
daily bread.

#### <a id="s6-9-e-6"></a>E.6 The afflicted

**Prayer.** Thou knowest also the great weakness of man’s nature, and wilt therefore
temper thy great wrath with mercy, for the sake of the merit and intercession of thy most dear
Son Jesus Christ our Lord. Therefore we beseech thee that thou wouldest graciously temper our
well-deserved punishments, and comfort with thy Holy Spirit all the sorrowful that call upon
thee, that they may abide in right faith and right calling upon thee, and praise thy mercy for
ever. Amen.

---

### <a id="s6-10"></a>6.10 Family F: Upper German pulpit intercession (Strasbourg/Zürich)

Upper German (Bucerian/Zwinglian) intercession after the sermon, a continuous prayer with
rubrics, related to Zürich 1535 and the Strasbourg forms.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Augsburg 1537.
- **Tradition:** Moderate Reformed (Upper German, Bucerian).
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** continuous prayer with rubrics + Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Augsburg 1537):** At the end of the sermon service (after the
  Decalogue, confession, and the Creed); banns and requests for prayer are read within it.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1537 | Augsburg, Kirchenordnung (Die zehen gebot, Articul des Glaubens, Und das Vater unser) (Moderate Reformed) | Augsburg (Imperial city) | Sehling 12, I.8a, pp. 70–71 | prayer with rubrics + Lord’s Prayer |

**Sequence:** F.1 Exhortation / preface > F.2 All men > F.3 Civil authority > F.4 Ministers of
the Word > F.5 All estates / households > F.6 Special intercessions > F.7 Women with child > F.8
Schools & youth > F.9 All estates / households > F.10 The afflicted > F.11 Special
intercessions > F.12 The persecuted > F.13 The erring & unbelievers > F.14 Against the Turk >
F.15 Against the Turk > F.16 Lord's Prayer.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-1"></a>F.1 Exhortation / preface

**Rubric.** Intercession for the common estates:

**Bid.** But forasmuch as it is good and acceptable before God our Saviour, and he
hath commanded us by his holy Apostle to pray for all men, let us in his name, wherein all good
is promised us, come before God our gracious Father with true faith and hearty confidence, and
say thus:

#### <a id="s6-10-f-2"></a>F.2 All men

**Prayer.** Almighty, everlasting God, dear and faithful Father in heaven: as thy
great grace and goodness showeth itself richly toward all men, so, forasmuch as we are thy
children, we desire from our hearts to take after thy fatherly bounty as far as may be, and to
show forth our love toward all men in Christian wise by our faithful intercession, since we can
do no more; and we call upon thee therefore, through thy Son Jesus Christ, our dear Lord and
Saviour, for all the estates and concerns of thy holy Christendom.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-3"></a>F.3 Civil authority

**Prayer.** First for our lord the Emperor, the King, all princes, lords and rulers,
but especially for our worshipful magistrates in this city. Vouchsafe unto them all the spirit
of thy fear and wisdom, that they may order all their government to the praise and glory of thy
great name and to the peaceable preservation of the subjects in all honesty and godliness. But
unto the subjects give a willing and seemly heart to obey the magistrates in all that is not
against thee.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-4"></a>F.4 Ministers of the Word

**Prayer.** We beseech thee also from our hearts, grant unto all ministers and
preachers of thy holy word that with sound doctrine and unblameable life they may preside in
Christian wise over thy holy congregation to its daily amendment. But especially, faithful
Father, ordain graciously at all times all good means, that neither we nor our posterity may
ever lack faithful stewards of thy mysteries and of the comfortable Gospel of thy Son Jesus
Christ.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-5"></a>F.5 All estates / households

**Prayer.** Have mercy also, gracious God, upon all fathers and mothers of households,
and also schoolmasters and all that have children or servants, that they may bring them up and
govern them godly according to the direction of thy word, to thy praise and the profit of thy
Church. Let also, dear God, thy peace and blessing prevail richly over all married folk, that
they may dwell together in love and unity and bear all the burdens of wedlock with faith and
patience. But especially vouchsafe this unto these persons that desire to bind themselves
together in marriage, by name, etc.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-6"></a>F.6 Special intercessions

**Rubric.** Here the marriages shall be published, and then thereupon further said
thus:

**Prayer.** Grant them, merciful Father, to enter upon this holy estate in thy fear,
that they may also live therein in Christian wise and close the same blessedly.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-7"></a>F.7 Women with child

**Prayer.** Wilt thou also, O heavenly Father, graciously deliver women in travail and
gladden them graciously with a well-formed fruit, well-pleasing unto thee.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-8"></a>F.8 Schools & youth

**Prayer.** We pray thee also, gracious Father, for our youth not yet brought up, that
thou wouldest bring them up in fatherly wise by thy Holy Spirit and form them according to thy
will and good pleasure, that they may grow up blessedly in thy fear and in faith in thy Son
Jesus Christ, and that every service of thy congregation may evermore be well and christianly
supplied by them.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-9"></a>F.9 All estates / households

**Prayer.** Give thy gracious increase and blessing to all faithful servants and
labourers. Endow the poor with bodily sustenance and Christian resignation, the rich with
faithful liberality.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-10"></a>F.10 The afflicted

**Prayer.** Show thyself a faithful and bountiful Father to all sorrowful hearts,
tempted within or without. Grant unto the sick long-suffering patience, to the dying a joyful
going up to heaven. And in especial have mercy upon certain which at this time in their
suffering, sickness and tribulation desire our intercession.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-11"></a>F.11 Special intercessions

**Rubric.** Here he shall announce them that desire the common prayer, and thereupon
say:

**Prayer.** Let all that befall them in fatherly wise, faithful God, which according
to thy will they desire to obtain of thee through our intercession. Give them the comfort of thy
grace, that in the midst of suffering and tribulation they may feel thy fatherly heart in true
faith and bring forth much fruit in patience. Strengthen all the fainthearted and weak in faith.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-12"></a>F.12 The persecuted

**Prayer.** Uphold with thy mighty hand all that for thy name’s and for righteousness’
sake suffer imprisonment and persecution under the cruel Turk or otherwise.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-13"></a>F.13 The erring & unbelievers

**Prayer.** Show and lead all that err into the way of Christian truth and of eternal
life. Enlighten all the blinded. Soften all the hardened. Bring back all that are fallen away
from the Christian faith and the unity of thy Church. Drive out unbelief from the hearts of all
men, that thy kingdom may daily come more and more, and thine only-begotten Son, our dear Lord
and Saviour Jesus Christ, be known to the whole world and be lauded and praised of it.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-14"></a>F.14 Against the Turk

**Rubric.** Against the Turk and the persecutors of the Gospel

**Bid.** Include also therewith the horrible hereditary enemy of the Christian name,
the Turk; praying that almighty God would smite him with the breath of his Holy Spirit, that the
name of Jesus Christ be not blasphemed by him, nor so much Christian blood shed by him. For this
and all other need of the whole of Christendom, and also for ourselves and for all for whom we
are bound to pray, we will pray to God with hearty humility, not with the mouth only but with
the whole heart, and say thus: Our Father, etc.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-15"></a>F.15 Against the Turk

**Rubric.** Or thus:

**Prayer.** Wilt thou also, O faithful God and Father, with thine almighty power
withstand the might of the tyrannous, antichristian kingdom of the Turk, which setteth itself
wantonly against Christ, together with all idolatry, tyranny and ungodly being, and cast it down
to be the footstool of Christ’s feet; that thy divine name, together with the faith of Christ in
us, be not mocked and reviled by the unbelieving people and the enemies of the truth, but be
enlarged and spread abroad by thy Holy Spirit, and the enemy be driven back through Christ
Jesus.

#### <a id="s6-10-f-16"></a>F.16 Lord's Prayer

**Rubric.** The Our Father followeth:

**Bid.** In his name, O faithful, gracious and merciful Father, and at his bidding, we
come before thy face and call upon thee, as our Lord Jesus Christ himself hath taught and
commanded us to pray, and say:

**Prayer.** Our Father, which art in the heavens. Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom
come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and
forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us
from evil: for thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.

---

### <a id="s6-11"></a>6.11 Family G: Hessian Vermanung zum Gebet

Hessian "Vermanung zum Gebet" (Exhortation to prayer): a numbered bidding exhortation which the order allows to be
shortened or lengthened locally.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Hessen 1566.
- **Tradition:** Moderate Reformed (Philip of Hesse's church).
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** numbered bidding exhortation.
- **Place in the service (Hessen 1566):** The fifth part of the service: after the Creed and the
  sermon, “the prayer for all manner of estates and all manner of pressing need of the church”, justified from
  Justin Martyr (Apol. I 65) and Tertullian (Apol. 30–39).

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1566 | Hessen, Kirchenordnung 1566 (Moderate Reformed) | Landgraviate of Hesse | Sehling 8, I/Hessen Nr. 17 (KO 1566), pp. 245–246 | bidding exhortation (numbered) |

**Sequence:** G.1 Exhortation / preface > G.2 Ministers of the Word > G.3 Civil authority > G.4
The erring & unbelievers > G.5 Enemies > G.6 The afflicted > G.7 Deliverance from calamities >
G.8 Conclusion > G.9 Special intercessions.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-1"></a>G.1 Exhortation / preface

**Rubric.** But the minister of the word may exhort the whole church to prayer on this
wise: (in the margin: Exhortation to prayer)

**Bid.** Dearly beloved in the Lord, there is no man but knoweth and understandeth, so
soon as he asketh his own conscience, that he needeth the help, benefits, grace and mercy of God
at all times and in all places; for we are all of us poor, weak and frail men. But we are taught
of the Lord Christ that we should ask and look for all good, yea, whatsoever is profitable and
needful for us, from our heavenly Father alone, who ever knoweth what we need, with an humble
and penitent heart out of true faith. Moreover, if we will witness that there is in us a spark
of brotherly and unfeigned love, we are bound by the commandment and example of Christ to pray
for others also, and not only for them that wish us well and do us good, but also for all
estates of men, yea, also for our enemies and persecutors, and for whatsoever need besides. And
how we should make our prayer unto God in common, all the God-fearing are instructed by the
Spirit of God. Over and above all this we have a commandment from Christ that we should
steadfastly ask in his name of his heavenly Father, who is, and will be known of all men as a
gracious Lord and true almighty God and Father, who easily can and also will graciously give us
all that is profitable and wholesome. Our Lord Christ hath also promised us that whatsoever we
shall ask the heavenly Father in his name, he will give it us willingly and richly. Lastly, we
know also from the promise of Christ that the prayer of every believer, to say nothing of the
whole congregation lawfully gathered in the name of Christ, shall be heard for Christ’s sake.
Whence it followeth undeniably that the common prayer is a special mark and exercise of the
Christian Church and of all believers, which is well-pleasing and acceptable unto almighty God.
Therefore we also in this our assembly, with one mind in the Spirit and in truth, call upon God
the Lord not only for ourselves but also for the whole Church and all estates and necessities of
men:

#### <a id="s6-11-g-2"></a>G.2 Ministers of the Word

**Bid.** First and before all things for all ministers of God’s word and for the happy
course of the Gospel, that the same may be planted and spread abroad in all lands, and so the
number of the believers in Christ may grow and increase, as we have commandment thereof from
Christ and the Apostle Paul: namely, that utterance may be given unto the preachers to proclaim
the word with the joyful opening of their mouth, that the mystery of the Gospel of Christ may be
made known and manifest, and that they may deal and speak boldly therein, as it becometh, to the
furtherance and joy of the faith of the congregation; and that unto the Church and congregation
the grace in the Holy Ghost may be given in Christ, that she may be enriched in all doctrine and
all knowledge, as the preaching of Christ becometh mighty in her, so that she come behind in no
gift, and walk unblameably and worthily of the Gospel of Christ, and so stand fast in one spirit
and in one soul, striving for the faith of the Gospel, and be in nothing terrified by the
adversaries, but hold fast to the Gospel unto the end and wait for the revelation of Jesus
Christ.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-3"></a>G.3 Civil authority

**Bid.** Secondly, we will also pray for the Emperor, kings, princes, magistrates and
all in authority, and for a quiet government and common peace, as is commanded us by the Apostle
in Timothy 2.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-4"></a>G.4 The erring & unbelievers

**Bid.** Thirdly, for all them that long for the knowledge of the truth, be they who
they will; and also them that in foreign lands are persecuted and martyred for the truth’s sake.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-5"></a>G.5 Enemies

**Bid.** Fourthly, we will also pray for all our adversaries and persecutors, but
chiefly for them that out of ignorance resist the truth and persecute the Christians unjustly,
that God the Lord would graciously forgive them this and not impute this grievous sin unto them,
and that he would lead such to the knowledge of the truth, that they also may be saved.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-6"></a>G.6 The afflicted

**Bid.** Fifthly, for all the sick and them that have an inward or outward temptation,
and also for all that are sorrowful by reason of the cross which God sendeth them, that they may
be comforted, as we read in the Epistle of James, chapter 5.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-7"></a>G.7 Deliverance from calamities

**Bid.** Sixthly, we will also call upon God especially for the present common
necessity. This petition is needful when war, hunger or dearth, or else other need and mishaps
are at hand.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-8"></a>G.8 Conclusion

**Bid.** Seventhly, let us also pray for all that concerneth the whole Christian
congregation, for all for which God will be called upon. We will also pray one for another, for
ourselves that are here come together. And let us first forgive one another, and thereafter call
upon God and pray for grace and forgiveness of sins.

#### <a id="s6-11-g-9"></a>G.9 Special intercessions

**Rubric.** This form of prayer may be made shorter or longer, according to the
circumstances of each church.

---

### <a id="s6-12"></a>6.12 Family H: Bugenhagen pulpit exhortation

Bugenhagen's pulpit exhortation after the sermon in Low German: the people are led through
Creed, confession, biddings for all estates and needs, and the Our Father. Hamburg copies it
verbatim; Osnabrück prescribes the same contents in indirect speech.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Braunschweig 1528 (Bugenhagen).
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** Low German.
- **Form:** pulpit exhortation: Creed, confession, biddings, Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Braunschweig 1528):** From the pulpit after the sermon (“exhortation or admonition from the pulpit after the sermon”); the exhortation to communicants before
  the altar follows.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1528 | Braunschweig, Der erbarn stadt Brunswig christlike ordeninge (Bugenhagen) | Braunschweig (city) | Sehling 6/1, I/1, p. 443 | exhortation: Creed + confession + biddings + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1529 | Hamburg, Kirchenordnung (Bugenhagen) | Hamburg (city) | Sehling 5, Hamburg mit Landgebiet, pp. 530–531 | exhortation: Creed + confession + biddings + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1543 | Stift Osnabrück, Kirchenordnung (Hermann Bonnus): Ordenunge der evangelischen missen | Prince-Bishopric (Stift) and city of Osnabrück | Sehling 7/1, III/Stift Osnabrück, pp. 224–225 | prescription of contents (indirect speech) |

Osnabrück 1543 prescribes the contents in indirect speech. It supplies H.3 and H.5.

**Not in the representative text** (a minority reading of its category; see the Prayers sheet or
the critical sheets): Osnabrück 1543 no. 2 (Civil authority).

**Sequence:** H.1 Creed > H.2 Confession of sins > H.3 The Word & its fruit > H.4 Civil
authority > H.5 The present congregation > H.6 Ministers of the Word > H.7 Peace > H.8 Lord's
Prayer > H.9 Special intercessions.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-1"></a>H.1 Creed

*Witnesses:* Braunschweig 1528 and Hamburg 1529.

**Rubric.** Exhortation or admonition from the pulpit after the sermon:

**Bid.** Dear friends in Christ, say with me the Creed. I believe in God the Father
Almighty, etc.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-2"></a>H.2 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Braunschweig 1528 and Hamburg 1529.

**Bid.** Say also the confession with me, and confess your sins unto God, that God may
be gracious unto us.

**Prayer.** God be merciful to me a poor sinner. I fail in faith, in that I love not
God my Lord with my whole heart, nor trust wholly in him in temptations and in all need of body
and soul. I ought to fear God alone and have him before mine eyes in all things; but now I fear
the people that can do me evil for righteousness’ sake. I fear to lose my goods, honour,
friendship and life. I care for my living in unchristian wise, and seek in all things mine own,
and not the things that are God’s. Neither do I set my salvation wholly in Jesus Christ, his
only-begotten Son, given for us. I fail also in love, in that I love not my neighbour as myself,
but deal against him with evil suspicions, with backbiting, with words, with works, and can bear
no word from him against me. I keep silence then the more, and cannot forgive him from the
heart, and yet am bound to do so. Especially I have a burdened conscience in this temptation:
N., in this sin: N. (Let every one bewail unto God his secret, grievous sin, unto amendment.)
Therefore, almighty God, dear Father, forgive me all my sins, and enlighten my heart with thy
truth, that I may hold thee for my gracious Father, and my neighbour for my brother, without all
offence, according to thy word; through our Lord Jesus Christ. (Say:) Amen. Jesus Christ is our
salvation for ever. (Say:) Amen.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-3"></a>H.3 The Word & its fruit

*Witnesses:* Osnabrück 1543.

**Bid.** After the exposition of the Gospel the pastor shall say over the words of the
catechism for the sake of the common people, and thereafter exhort them to pray: first, for the
cause of the holy Gospel;

#### <a id="s6-12-h-4"></a>H.4 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Braunschweig 1528 and Hamburg 1529.

**Bid.** Let us now pray diligently for the Imperial Majesty, for kings, for lords,
princes, princes’ counsellors and town councillors, noblemen, burgomasters and judges, and all
to whom the temporal sword is committed, especially for our prince of the land and for the
council of this city, that God may be always with them with his grace, and grant them that they
may rule unblameably in the temporal things that are committed unto them, that we under them may
lead a quiet and still life in all godliness and honesty.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-5"></a>H.5 The present congregation

*Witnesses:* Osnabrück 1543.

**Bid.** thirdly, for the whole congregation and for all other need of body and soul,
wherefor it is desired and is known to God. Thereafter shall be sung: Grant us peace graciously.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-6"></a>H.6 Ministers of the Word

*Witnesses:* Braunschweig 1528 and Hamburg 1529.

**Bid.** Pray ye also for the priests that feed us poor sheep with the word and Gospel
of Christ, that they may set forth unto us the pure word of God with a steadfast heart to our
amendment, and be kept from all error and strengthened unto all good against the devil and all
gainsayers, that the Gospel of Christ may ever remain pure among us.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-7"></a>H.7 Peace

*Witnesses:* Braunschweig 1528 and Hamburg 1529.

**Bid.** Pray ye also for temporal peace; for the sick, the weak, the wretched and
tempted folk; for women with child; for our enemies; for all need of body and soul. Amen. Let us
pray one for another, that we may all be saved. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-8"></a>H.8 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Braunschweig 1528 and Hamburg 1529.

**Bid.** Say an Our Father, etc.

#### <a id="s6-12-h-9"></a>H.9 Special intercessions

*Witnesses:* Braunschweig 1528 and Hamburg 1529.

**Rubric.** If any special common needs befall, as to pray for the corn, hops, fruits,
for seasonable weather, against evil murrain and pestilence, etc., that may well be brought in
therewith.

---

### <a id="s6-13"></a>6.13 Family I: Huberinus Vorbitt (Lord’s-Prayer order)

Caspar Huberinus' "Vorbitt" (intercession), whose first part is arranged by the petitions of the Lord's Prayer.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Öhringen 1544 (Huberinus).
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** bidding exhortation + Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Öhringen 1544):** After the sermon; closes with the Our Father, a
  declaration that the prayer is heard, and a reminder of the alms.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1544 | Öhringen (Hohenlohe), Vermahnungen und Gebete für den Gottesdienst (Caspar Huberinus) | County of Hohenlohe (Öhringen) | Sehling 15, Nr. 3 (Vermahnungen und Gebete 1544–1550), pp. 39–40 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |

**Sequence:** I.1 Exhortation / preface > I.2 Civil authority > I.3 The persecuted > I.4 Peace >
I.5 Repentance & forgiveness > I.6 Women with child > I.7 Special intercessions > I.8 Lord's
Prayer > I.9 Conclusion.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-1"></a>I.1 Exhortation / preface

**Rubric.** A short exhortation and intercession, to pray for the Christian estates

**Bid.** Forasmuch as we are now here gathered together according to God’s
commandment, to hear his wholesome word and thereafter also to make our prayer unto God the Lord
in the name of Christ for all manner of pressing need of the whole of Christendom, we will call
upon God the Almighty, our heavenly Father, out of childlike confidence with believing hearts,
and pray him that he would graciously hear and grant us, for the sake of his divine truth and
promise which hath been made us by his dear Son: that God the Lord would first and chiefly, out
of fatherly faithfulness, impart, vouchsafe, defend and preserve unto us his holy word, the
gracious Gospel, that we may preach, hear and obey the same purely and clearly with right
understanding, that thereby his name may be hallowed and praised among us and in all the world.
That God the Lord would also root out all false doctrine, error and heresy, and graciously keep
us therefrom, that his kingdom may come to us and rule us with his word, grace and Holy Spirit,
whereby the kingdom of Satan, of Mahomet and of Antichrist may come to an end and be laid waste
and destroyed; that so his fatherly will may be done, not the will of the flesh, the world and
Satan, but his will be done here among us on earth as above in heaven. Moreover, that God
Almighty would everywhere ordain, preserve, defend and guard all faithful bishops, pastors,
preachers and ministers of the Church.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-2"></a>I.2 Civil authority

**Bid.** We will also pray for the Christian magistrates, for the Imperial and Royal
Majesty, for all Electors, princes, lords and all the estates of the Empire. But especially let
us pray for our protecting lords and potentates, and likewise for their counsellors, officers
and servants. God the Lord give them all together the true fear of God, wisdom and understanding
to rule blessedly and well, that under their government we may yet longer have God’s word,
temporal peace and sustenance.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-3"></a>I.3 The persecuted

**Bid.** We will also call upon God especially further and pray him for worthy
Christendom, which everywhere is oppressed, afflicted and persecuted by the unbelievers, the
Turk, Mahometan, antichristian, bloodthirsty people: that God would graciously defend and
deliver the poor Christians and keep them in the right faith.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-4"></a>I.4 Peace

**Bid.** Let us also pray for all Christian subjects, that God the Lord would
graciously keep them in due duty and obedience and guard them from discord and uproar, and so
defend and preserve us all in fatherly wise from war, bloodshed, dearth, sickness, pestilence,
hail, storm, hurtful tempest, from all vermin, poisoned air and the like, that we may receive
our daily bread in all stillness, peace, rest and health.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-5"></a>I.5 Repentance & forgiveness

**Bid.** Let us also pray that God the Lord would graciously forgive us our debt,
spare our frail life, not impute the old and former sins, but forgive them of grace in Christ
our Lord; that he would also give us such an heart that we can forgive from the right ground
them that grudge against us and our enemies, that we may have a loving heart toward our
neighbour. That God the Lord would also not lead us into temptation nor let us fall into trial,
but keep us of grace, that we fall not into the hurtful temptation and enticement of the flesh,
the world and Satan; but that God Almighty would deliver us from evil, from all harm of body and
soul, temporal and eternal.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-6"></a>I.6 Women with child

**Bid.** In especial let us pray for all women with child and in travail, for widows
and orphans, for the dear youth, for married folk, especially where the evil enemy hath sown his
seed, discord, bitterness and disunity; that neighbours also may show themselves one toward
another united, peaceable, well-willing, serviceable and loving.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-7"></a>I.7 Special intercessions

**Bid.** Pray ye in conclusion for certain sick, tempted, fainthearted and comfortless
persons, which commend themselves faithfully in especial to your Christian prayer. Pray ye also
for them for whom we are especially bound to pray, which are commended to us in our office and
prayer.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-8"></a>I.8 Lord's Prayer

**Bid.** For this and all other need of the whole of Christendom, and also for
ourselves and ours, we will call upon God the Lord from the heart. Therefore make your prayer to
God Almighty in the name of our Lord with your whole heart, and pray with devotion, inwardly,
from the heart, an Our Father.

#### <a id="s6-13-i-9"></a>I.9 Conclusion

**Rubric.** After the prayer, the conclusion:

**Prayer.** Almighty God hath graciously heard our prayer according to his divine
promise, in Christ our Lord. To him be laud, honour, glory and praise, now and for ever. Amen.
Let the poor and needy be faithfully commended to you in your almsgiving.

---

### <a id="s6-14"></a>6.14 Family J: Lower Saxon notel (Lüneburg/Wolfenbüttel)

Lower Saxon exhortation to prayer read "from the notel" after the sermon; passed verbatim to
Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Lüneburg 1564.
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** bidding exhortation + Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Lüneburg 1564):** At the end of the sermon (never between the Gospel
  reading and its exposition, except for a woman in childbirth or one in peril of death); the
  communicants then come into the choir and kneel.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1564 | Braunschweig-Lüneburg (Celle), Kirchenordnung 1564 | Duchy of Braunschweig-Lüneburg (Lüneburg) | Sehling 6/1, II/4, pp. 545–546 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1569 | Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel, Kirchenordnung (Herzog Julius; Chemnitz/Andreae) | Duchy of Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel | Sehling 6/1, I/3, pp. 145–146 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1573 | Oldenburg, Kirchenordnung 1573 (Graf Anton I.) | County of Oldenburg | Sehling 7/2, VI/Oldenburg Nr. 26 (KO 1573), pp. 1146–1147 | bidding exhortation + Lord’s Prayer |

The magistrates are prayed for twice: for the Emperor and all magistrates (J.2), and, after a
thanksgiving for the princes of the land, for the princess and the young lordship (J.4).

**Sequence:** J.1 The Word & its fruit > J.2 Civil authority > J.3 Thanksgiving > J.4 Civil
authority > J.5 The afflicted > J.6 Deliverance from calamities > J.7 Lord's Prayer > J.8
Special intercessions.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-1"></a>J.1 The Word & its fruit

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Rubric.** Thereupon the people shall again be exhorted to prayer and thanksgiving
toward God, and all together for the preservation of the Church of God and of right doctrine,
and moreover of the faithful, true teachers, and that God would send faithful labourers into his
harvest; for the magistrates, for temporal peace and the growth of the fruits; and in sum for
the need of the whole of Christendom and of particular persons that desire the Christian prayer;
whereof a draft followeth, after this manner.

**Bid.** Dear Christians, let us pray God that he would graciously keep us in his
divine word, and send faithful labourers into his harvest; vouchsafe his Holy Spirit unto the
preachers and ministers of the Church, that they may set forth and teach the same purely and
rightly, and also go before with godly life; and that the Almighty would graciously keep them
and us from false doctrine, and restrain and withstand the same. That he would also graciously
help our brethren and sisters which are assailed and oppressed with false doctrine or else with
unrighteous violence by unchristian men or other tyrants, that they may abide steadfast in true
faith and patience, and, if it be possible, that the persecution may be taken from them or
mitigated.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-2"></a>J.2 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Bid.** Pray ye also for the temporal magistrates, the Imperial Majesty and other
potentates, and all others that sit in the office of magistracy: that the Almighty would
graciously keep therein them that are enlightened by God’s word, but give his grace unto them
that are not yet enlightened, that they may suffer and receive God’s word in their lands; but
that he would restrain them that will not do so and persecute it, and bring their purpose to
shame.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-3"></a>J.3 Thanksgiving

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Bid.** Especially give thanks to God that he hath so graced our gracious princes and
lords of the land that they love God’s word and let it be preached and further it in their land;
and pray that the Almighty would graciously keep them therein and vouchsafe him godly long life,
health and grace, that they may so lead their government that it may redound to the honour of
God and to the good of their princely Graces and their subjects, and that we may lead a quiet,
peaceable life under them in all godliness.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-4"></a>J.4 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Bid.** Pray ye also for our gracious princess of the land, that the Almighty would
have her also in his gracious protection, guard her from all mischief, and bless her in body and
soul. Pray ye also for the counsellors, officers and governors, and also the council of this
town, that God would give them grace to counsel well and faithfully to preside over and perform
the offices and charges committed unto them.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-5"></a>J.5 The afflicted

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Bid.** Pray ye also for all tempted and sorrowful hearts, for all the sick, women
with child, young children, and all that are in need, that the Almighty would comfort and guard
them all, and stand by them and come to their help in their needs.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-6"></a>J.6 Deliverance from calamities

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Bid.** Pray ye for us all in this congregation and in the whole land, that God would
be gracious unto us and keep us from war, pestilence and dearth, from fire and flood, from hail
and tempest, and from all mischance and evil; and that he would guard the fruits upon the field
and give blessing and grace, that we may enjoy them with peace, health and thanksgiving.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-7"></a>J.7 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Bid.** Let every one lay his own need before God, and pray ye in the name of Christ
upon his promise, where he saith: Whatsoever ye ask in my name, believe, and ye shall have it;
and say from the ground of the heart: Our Father, etc.

#### <a id="s6-14-j-8"></a>J.8 Special intercessions

*Witnesses:* Lüneburg 1564, Braunschweig-Wolfenbüttel 1569 and Oldenburg 1573.

**Rubric.** If then aught befall whereof special petition is to be made, as for
particular sick persons, for women that are in the pains of childbirth, and whatsoever else of
need and matters of the land or of particular persons may befall, that shall be added to this
common prayer also in short words.

---

### <a id="s6-15"></a>6.15 Family K: Three collects from the pulpit

After an exhortation the minister reads three collects from the pulpit: thanksgiving or the
Church, the magistrates, and a special need, chosen from a bank.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Worms 1560.
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** exhortation + three collects.
- **Place in the service (Worms 1560):** On Sundays and feasts, when the choir has finished the
  first psalm or hymn, the minister goes into the pulpit, exhorts the people to prayer and reads
  three collects: (1) a thanksgiving for God’s gifts or a prayer for the preservation of the
  Church and God’s word (on feasts, a thanksgiving for the feast), (2) for the magistrates, (3) a
  special prayer as the time requires (peace, protection, fruits of the earth, rain …).

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1560 | Worms, Agendbüchlein 1560 | Worms (Imperial city) | Sehling 19, III/4, pp. 178–183 | exhortation + three collects |

Worms reads three collects from the pulpit: a thanksgiving, or a prayer for the Church and God's
word; one for the magistrates; and a third that varies with the time, chosen from the collect
bank that follows in the order. K.2 and K.3 are the two texts for the first collect, K.4 is the
collect for the magistrates, and K.5 is the rubric for the third.

**Sequence:** K.1 Exhortation / preface > K.2 Thanksgiving > K.3 The Church > K.4 Civil
authority > K.5 Special intercessions.

#### <a id="s6-15-k-1"></a>K.1 Exhortation / preface

**Rubric.** VI. Of the common prayer. Although at the end of all sermons the people
are sufficiently exhorted to pray earnestly and diligently for all the need and concerns of the
whole of Christendom in the spiritual, temporal and household government, and also to
thankfulness toward God for his great and manifold benefits, yet for the sake of greater
remembrance certain other common prayers and collects are also held and read plainly to the
people in the following order. On Sundays and feast days, when the choir hath finished the first
psalm or spiritual song, the minister goeth into the pulpit and exhorteth the people to prayer,
and readeth to them three collects at a time. The first is either a common thanksgiving for all
manner of God’s gifts, or a prayer for the preservation of the Church and God’s word, or, if it
be on special feasts, a thanksgiving for those special gifts whereof it is wont to be treated on
that feast. The second is of the temporal magistrates. The third is special, according to the
occasion of the time: either for peace, or for protection, or for the fruits of the earth, or
for rain, etc., and whatsoever like special need and concern may befall, whereof the Christian
Church must be put in mind, out of the register following.

#### <a id="s6-15-k-2"></a>K.2 Thanksgiving

**Rubric.** A common thanksgiving for all manner of benefits of God.

**Prayer.** Almighty Lord God, heavenly Father, of whom we without ceasing receive all
manner of good right abundantly, and are daily kept from all evil stately and graciously: we
beseech thee, give us by thy Spirit to acknowledge all this with our whole heart in right faith,
that we may thank thy bountiful goodness and mercy here and there eternally, and praise thee;
through our Lord Jesus Christ thy dear Son, etc.

#### <a id="s6-15-k-3"></a>K.3 The Church

**Rubric.** For the preservation and fruitful increase of God’s word.

**Prayer.** Almighty God, we beseech thee, give unto thy congregation thy Spirit and
divine wisdom, that thy word may run and grow among us and be preached with all boldness, as it
becometh, and that thy holy Christian congregation may be bettered thereby; that we may serve
thee with steadfast faith and continue in the confession of thy name unto the end; through our
Lord, etc.

#### <a id="s6-15-k-4"></a>K.4 Civil authority

**Rubric.** For the temporal magistrates alone.

**Prayer.** O merciful heavenly Father, in whose hand standeth all power of men and
the welfare of the godly, in whose hand also stand all the rights and laws of all realms upon
earth: we beseech thee, look graciously upon thy servants, the Roman Emperor, all kings, princes
and Christian magistrates, that they may bear the temporal sword, committed unto them of thee,
according to thy commandment. Enlighten them and keep them in thy divine name; give them, dear
Lord, wisdom and understanding and a peaceable government, that they may defend and rule their
subjects in peace, rest and unity. Prolong their days, O God of our salvation, that under their
dominion we together with them may hallow and praise thy divine name; through our Lord Jesus
Christ, etc.

#### <a id="s6-15-k-5"></a>K.5 Special intercessions

**Rubric.** The third is special … out of the register following.

---

### <a id="s6-16"></a>6.16 Family L: Intercessions under the Sanctus (Brandenburg 1540)

Not a pulpit prayer but collects said by the priest in the Mass under the Sanctus, for
ministers, magistrates and peace, in the place the Roman Canon had its intercessions. Followed
by Calenberg-Göttingen 1542 and Pfalz-Neuburg 1543.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Brandenburg 1540.
- **Tradition:** Lutheran.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** collects said by the priest under the Sanctus.
- **Place in the service (Brandenburg 1540):** In the Mass, after the Preface, while the Latin
  Sanctus is sung; followed by the Verba (sung in German, with elevation) and the Our Father. The
  prayers stand where the Roman Canon had its intercessions.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1540 | Mark Brandenburg, Kirchenordnung (Kurfürst Joachim II.) | Electorate of Brandenburg | Sehling 3, Mark Brandenburg Nr. 3, pp. 68–69 | collects said by the priest |
| 1542 | Calenberg-Göttingen, Kirchenordnung (Herzogin Elisabeth; Corvinus) | Principality of Calenberg-Göttingen | Sehling 6/2, III/Calenberg-Göttingen, p. 815 | collect said by the priest |
| 1543 | Pfalz-Neuburg, Kirchenordnung (Pfalzgraf Ottheinrich; Osiander) | Palatinate-Neuburg | Sehling 13, I.2, p. 74 | collects said by the priest |

Each collect ends "through thy Son Jesus Christ. Amen." in place of the abbreviation "through our Lord etc." (Introduction, [Representative texts](#repo-prayers-rules), rule 4).

**Sequence:** L.1 Civil authority > L.2 Ministers of the Word > L.3 Peace > L.4 Repentance &
forgiveness > L.5 Lord's Prayer.

#### <a id="s6-16-l-1"></a>L.1 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Brandenburg 1540, Calenberg-Göttingen 1542 and Pfalz-Neuburg 1543.

**Rubric.** Under the Sanctus the priest shall pray the following prayer in German. ¶
For the magistrates.

**Prayer.** Merciful heavenly Father, in whose hands standeth all power and authority
of men, ordained of thee for the punishment of evildoers and the protection of the godly, in
whose hands also stand all the rights and laws of all lands: we beseech thee, be gracious unto
our lord the Emperor, all kings and princes, especially unto our prince and lord of the land N.,
and unto the council and rulers of this city and all lawful magistrates, that they may rightly
bear the temporal sword which thou hast committed unto them. Overshadow them with the power of
the Highest; enlighten them and keep them in thy divine name; let them love thy divine word from
the heart and hold fast thereto, and in no wise suffer it to be persecuted. Give them, dear
Lord, wisdom and understanding and a peaceable government, that they may rule and defend all
their subjects in the truth and righteousness that is well-pleasing unto thee. Also, my dear
God, prolong their life according to thy will; and forasmuch as the judgement is thine and they
sit in thy stead, give them grace so to rule that thy holy name may be hallowed and praised
through them, from henceforth even for ever. This help them the Lord Jesus Christ, thy beloved
Son. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-16-l-2"></a>L.2 Ministers of the Word

*Witnesses:* Brandenburg 1540 and Pfalz-Neuburg 1543.

**Rubric.** Another.

**Prayer.** O almighty, gracious God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hast
earnestly commanded us that we should pray thee for labourers into thine harvest, that is, for
right and true preachers of thy word: we beseech thy bottomless mercy that thou wouldest send us
right and true teachers and ministers of thy divine word, and give thy wholesome word into their
heart and into their mouth, that they may faithfully perform thy commandment and preach nothing
that is contrary to thy holy word; to the end that we, being by thy heavenly, eternal word
admonished, taught, fed, comforted and strengthened, may do that which is well-pleasing unto
thee and profitable unto us. Give, O Lord, unto thy holy Christian Church thy Spirit and divine
wisdom, that thy word may run and grow among us and be preached with all boldness, as it
becometh, and that thy holy Christian congregation may be bettered thereby; that we may serve
thee with steadfast faith and continue in the knowledge of thy name unto the end; through thy
Son Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-16-l-3"></a>L.3 Peace

*Witnesses:* Brandenburg 1540 and Pfalz-Neuburg 1543.

**Rubric.** Another.

**Prayer.** Almighty God and everlasting Father, a King of glory and a Lord of heaven
and of earth, by whose Spirit all things are governed, by whose providence all things are
ordered; thou art a God of peace, from whom alone unity cometh unto us: we beseech thee through
our Lord Jesus Christ that thou wouldest forgive us our sins and endue us with thy divine peace
and unity, that we may serve thy name in fear and trembling, and that thou mayest be praised of
us evermore. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-16-l-4"></a>L.4 Repentance & forgiveness

*Witnesses:* Brandenburg 1540.

**Prayer.** Merciful God and heavenly Father, whose mercy hath no end, who art
longsuffering, gracious and of great goodness and faithfulness, and forgivest all iniquity,
transgression and sin: we have, alas, sinned with our fathers, we have done amiss and dealt
wickedly and oftentimes provoked thee to wrath; against thee only have we sinned and done evil
in thy sight. But, Lord, remember not against us our former iniquities; let thy mercy speedily
be great upon us, for we are brought very low. Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of
thy name; deliver us and forgive us our sins; through thy Son Jesus Christ. Amen.

#### <a id="s6-16-l-5"></a>L.5 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Brandenburg 1540, Calenberg-Göttingen 1542 and Pfalz-Neuburg 1543.
*Calenberg-Göttingen 1542 lacks the rubric.*

**Rubric.** Thereupon the Pater noster shall be sung in German, as followeth.

**Bid.** Let us pray, as the Lord Christ Jesus hath commanded us, that out of right
confidence and trust we may be bold to say:

**Prayer.** Our Father, which art in heaven, hallowed be thy name, thy kingdom come,
thy will be done, as in heaven, so in earth; give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us
our debts, as we forgive our debtors; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil:
for thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever.

---

### <a id="s6-17"></a>6.17 Family M: Pulpit biddings in the Prone pattern

Early East Frisian pulpit biddings after the medieval Prone: three biddings, then Decalogue,
confession, Creed and Our Father.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Norden 1528.
- **Tradition:** Reformed
  (an early East Frisian evangelical order, printed by Sehling among the Reformed orders of East Frisia).
- **Language:** Low Dutch.
- **Form:** biddings, then Decalogue, confession, Creed, Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Norden 1528):** Every Sunday after the sermon :
  three biddings, then the Ten Commandments, a confession of sins, the Creed with a confession
  of faith, and the Our Father.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1528 | Norden (East Frisia), Gottesdienstordnung [ca. 1528] (Reformed) | Norden, County of East Frisia | Sehling 7/1, IV/Ostfriesland Nr. 6, p. 431 | biddings + Decalogue + confession + Creed + Lord’s Prayer |

**Sequence:** M.1 Civil authority > M.2 Ministers of the Word > M.3 Enemies > M.4 Ten
Commandments.

#### <a id="s6-17-m-1"></a>M.1 Civil authority

**Rubric.** This manner written hereafter is observed at Norden every Sunday after the
sermon.

**Bid.** I. Let us call upon and pray God, our heavenly Father, for our gracious lord
with his council and officers, and for all the magistracy of the world, that God would govern
them and let them govern according to his word and Spirit, unto the common welfare and peace.

#### <a id="s6-17-m-2"></a>M.2 Ministers of the Word

**Bid.** II. For all faithful ministers and shepherds of the sheep of Christ, that
they may set forth God’s word boldly and with one accord, and preach Christ crucified.

#### <a id="s6-17-m-3"></a>M.3 Enemies

**Bid.** III. Item, for all our enemies and all unbelievers: heathen, Jews, Turks and
false Christians, that God would enlighten them with his word and Spirit and give them good
shepherds. Let us confess our weakness and sins, which are made manifest to us out of God’s law
and commandments.

#### <a id="s6-17-m-4"></a>M.4 Ten Commandments

**Rubric.** The Ten Commandments. … I believe in God the Father … Our Father in the
heavens …

---

### <a id="s6-18"></a>6.18 Family R1: Heidelberg 1563 prayer

The Reformed Sunday prayer after the sermon: confession and absolution, a long continuous prayer
(fruit of the Word, ministers, magistrates, all men, the persecuted, the afflicted, the
congregation), then the Our Father. Copied in Moers, Bentheim-Tecklenburg, Ysenburg-Birstein
1598 and, abridged, Lutheran Schaumburg 1614.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Kurpfalz 1563 (Heidelberg).
- **Tradition:** Reformed (Schaumburg 1614 Lutheran).
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** confession + absolution + continuous prayer + Our Father.
- **Place in the service (Kurpfalz 1563):** Sunday morning after the sermon: exhortation to
  confession, confession, absolution (with retention), then the prayer and the Our Father; a psalm
  and the Aaronic blessing follow. The prayer before the sermon is a separate confession of sins.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1563 | Kurpfalz, Kirchenordnung (Friedrich III.) (Reformed) | Electoral Palatinate | Sehling 14, Regierungszeit Friedrichs III. Nr. 60 (KO 1563), pp. 389–390 | confession + absolution + continuous prayer + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1581 | Moers, Kirchenordnung [1581] (Graf Adolf von Neuenahr) (Reformed) | County of Moers | Sehling 22, III/Moers Nr. 5 (KO [1581]), pp. 182–183 | continuous prayer + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1588 | Bentheim-Tecklenburg, Kirchenordnung 1588/1619 (Reformed) | Counties of Bentheim, Tecklenburg and Steinfurt | Sehling 22, IV/3, pp. 256–257 | continuous prayer + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1598 | Ysenburg-Birstein, Kirchenordnung 1598 (Graf Wolfgang Ernst) (Reformed) | County of Ysenburg-Büdingen-Birstein | Sehling 10, III/Ysenburg-Birstein Nr. 17, pp. 664–666 | confession + absolution + continuous prayer + Lord’s Prayer |
| 1614 | Schaumburg, Kirchenordnung 1614 (Graf/Fürst Ernst) (Lutheran) | County of Holstein-Schaumburg | Sehling 7/2.2, I/21, pp. 147–149 | confession + absolution + continuous prayer |

Schaumburg 1614 is a Lutheran order that takes over the Heidelberg confession, absolution and
prayer, abridged.

**Not in the representative text** (a minority reading of its category; see the Prayers sheet or
the critical sheets): Schaumburg 1614 no. 7 (Fruits of the earth).

**Sequence:** R1.1 Confession of sins > R1.2 Confession of sins > R1.3 Thanksgiving > R1.4 The
Word & its fruit > R1.5 Civil authority > R1.6 Fruits of the earth > R1.7 All men > R1.8 The
persecuted > R1.9 The afflicted > R1.10 Lord's Prayer.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-1"></a>R1.1 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Ysenburg-Birstein 1598 and Schaumburg 1614.

**Rubric.** On Sunday after the morning sermon the minister shall say:

**Bid.** Dearly beloved in the Lord, forasmuch as we see in the commandments of God as
in a glass how great and manifold our sins are, whereby we deserve temporal and eternal
punishment, let us confess the same from the heart unto our faithful Father; say therefore with
me thus:

**Prayer.** I, poor sinner, confess before thee, my God and Creator, that I, alas,
have sinned grievously and manifoldly against thee, not only with outward gross sins, but much
more with inward, inborn blindness, unbelief, doubting, faintheartedness, impatience, pride,
evil covetousness, secret envy, hatred and grudging, and other evil wiles, as thou, my Lord and
God, knowest in me, and I, alas, cannot sufficiently know; they repent me and grieve me, and I
desire grace from my heart, through thy dear Son Jesus Christ.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-2"></a>R1.2 Confession of sins

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Ysenburg-Birstein 1598 and Schaumburg 1614. *Schaumburg 1614 lacks
the rubric.*

**Rubric.** Thereupon he shall declare unto the faithful the forgiveness of sins, and
unto the impenitent the judgement of God, and say thus:

**Prayer.** Hear now the sure comfort of the grace of God, which he promiseth in his
Gospel to all believers. Thus saith the Lord Christ in John the third: God so loved the world,
that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have
everlasting life. As many of you therefore as are displeased with yourselves and your sins, and
trust that they are wholly and altogether forgiven them through the merit of Jesus Christ alone,
and have the purpose more and more to cease from sins and to serve the Lord in true holiness and
righteousness, unto them (forasmuch as they believe in the Son of the living God) I declare by
the commandment of God that they are loosed in heaven from all their sins (as he promiseth in
his holy Gospel) through the perfect satisfaction of the most holy suffering and death of our
Lord Jesus Christ. Amen. But as many among you as yet have pleasure in their sins and shame, or
continue in sins against their conscience, unto them I declare by the commandment of God that
the wrath and judgement of God abideth upon them, and that all their sins are retained in
heaven, and that they cannot be loosed from eternal damnation until they be converted.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-3"></a>R1.3 Thanksgiving

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588, Ysenburg-Birstein 1598 and
Schaumburg 1614. *Ysenburg-Birstein 1598 lacks the rubric.* *Moers 1581 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg
1588 lack the bid.*

**Rubric.** Prayer on Sunday after the sermon and absolution.

**Bid.** Forasmuch now as we doubt not that we and our prayer are sanctified through
the suffering of Jesus Christ and acceptable unto God, let us call upon him from the heart and
say thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty God, Creator of heaven and of earth, we give thee thanks from the
ground of our heart that thou hast created us, and unto this day hast preserved, fed and
nourished us and our children, and wilt yet henceforth preserve and govern us. But especially we
give thee thanks that thou hast given us to know thy Son Jesus Christ, whom thou didst promise
in Paradise, and hast forgiven us our sins through his bitter suffering and death.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-4"></a>R1.4 The Word & its fruit

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588 and Ysenburg-Birstein 1598.

**Prayer.** And we beseech thee that thou wouldest renew us unto the image of thy Son
Jesus Christ through the preaching of thy word and the power of thy Holy Spirit, that we may
live with thee eternally in body and soul and praise thee, whereunto we were created in the
beginning; and that thou wouldest withstand Satan, that he snatch not thy holy word out of our
hearts, as he did to our first parents Adam and Eve.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-5"></a>R1.5 Civil authority

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588, Ysenburg-Birstein 1598 and
Schaumburg 1614.

**Prayer.** And forasmuch as thou wilt govern us in this life also by the hand of our
magistrates, thy ministers, we beseech thee, who hast their hearts in thy hand, that thou
wouldest vouchsafe unto them all, the Imperial and royal Majesty, all princes and lords,
especially our most gracious Elector and prince of this land, Duke Frederick, Count Palatine,
together with his Electoral Grace’s consort, the young lordship, counsellors and officers (and
also an honourable council of this city, or an honourable commune of this place), grace and
unity, that they may direct their whole government to this end, that our Lord Jesus Christ, unto
whom thou hast given all power in heaven and in earth, may reign over them and their subjects;
that the poor people, which are the creatures of thy hands and the sheep of thy pasture, for
whom also the Lord Jesus hath shed his blood, may be governed in all holiness and righteousness;
and that we also for thy sake may show them all due honour and faithfulness, and lead under them
an honest, peaceable and Christian life.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-6"></a>R1.6 Fruits of the earth

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588 and Ysenburg-Birstein 1598.

**Prayer.** Give also thy blessing and benediction to the fruit of the earth, that we
may thereby acknowledge thee as a Father and fountain of all mercy and good things.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-7"></a>R1.7 All men

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588, Ysenburg-Birstein 1598 and
Schaumburg 1614.

**Prayer.** We pray thee also not for ourselves only, but also for all men of the
whole world, that thou wouldest have mercy upon them all graciously;

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-8"></a>R1.8 The persecuted

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588 and Ysenburg-Birstein 1598.

**Prayer.** but especially upon them that are our fellow members in the body of Jesus
Christ and for thy truth’s sake suffer persecution from the Turk and the Pope. Restrain, O
Father of all grace, such raging of thine enemies, which persecute thy Son Jesus in his members,
and strengthen the persecuted with invincible steadfastness and the power of thy Holy Spirit,
that they may receive such persecution from thy hand with thanksgiving, and in their tribulation
feel such joy as passeth all understanding.

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-9"></a>R1.9 The afflicted

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588, Ysenburg-Birstein 1598 and
Schaumburg 1614.

**Prayer.** Comfort and strengthen all the poor, the captives, the sick, widows and
orphans, women with child, and troubled and tempted hearts, and give them thy peace;

#### <a id="s6-18-r1-10"></a>R1.10 Lord's Prayer

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563, Moers 1581, Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588 and Ysenburg-Birstein 1598.

**Prayer.** through our dear Lord Jesus Christ, who hath made us this sure promise:
Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it
you; and hath commanded us thereupon to pray thus: Our Father, etc.

---

### <a id="s6-19"></a>6.19 Family R2: Heidelberg Lord’s-Prayer paraphrase

The Heidelberg alternative prayer paraphrasing the Lord's Prayer clause by clause (after Geneva
and the Heidelberg Catechism qq. 122-127).

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Kurpfalz 1563, alternative.
- **Tradition:** Reformed.
- **Language:** German.
- **Form:** Lord's Prayer paraphrase.
- **Place in the service (Kurpfalz 1563):** Alternative (“Or thus”) to the Sunday prayer after
  the sermon (after confession and absolution); followed by the Our Father, a psalm and the
  blessing.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1563 | Kurpfalz, Kirchenordnung (Friedrich III.) (Reformed) | Electoral Palatinate | Sehling 14, Regierungszeit Friedrichs III. Nr. 60 (KO 1563), pp. 390–391 | Lord’s Prayer paraphrase |
| 1588 | Bentheim-Tecklenburg, Kirchenordnung 1588/1619 (Reformed) | Counties of Bentheim, Tecklenburg and Steinfurt | Sehling 22, IV/3, pp. 256–258 | Lord’s Prayer paraphrase + Creed |

Each rubric is the clause of the Lord's Prayer that the paragraph expounds. Sehling prints the
clauses in square brackets in Kurpfalz 1563. Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588 adds R2.9.

**Sequence:** R2.1 Exhortation / preface > R2.2 The Word & its fruit > R2.3 The Church > R2.4
All estates / households > R2.5 Fruits of the earth > R2.6 Repentance & forgiveness > R2.7 The
present congregation > R2.8 Conclusion > R2.9 Creed.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-1"></a>R2.1 Exhortation / preface

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588.

**Rubric.** Or thus:

**Prayer.** Almighty God, heavenly Father, who hast promised us that whatsoever we
shall ask thee in the name of thy beloved Son Jesus Christ, thou wilt surely give it us:

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-2"></a>R2.2 The Word & its fruit

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588. *The rubric is in Kurpfalz 1563 only.*

**Rubric.** Hallowed be thy name.

**Prayer.** We beseech thee that thou wouldest work in us by thy Holy Spirit, that we
may rightly know thee, and hallow, extol and praise thee in all thy works, wherein shineth thine
almightiness, wisdom, goodness, righteousness, mercy and truth; and that we also may so direct
our whole life, thoughts, words and works, that thy name be not blasphemed for our sakes, but
honoured and praised.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-3"></a>R2.3 The Church

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588. *The rubric is in Kurpfalz 1563 only.*

**Rubric.** Thy kingdom come.

**Prayer.** Rule us also so by the sceptre of thy word and the power of thy Holy
Spirit, that we and all men may from day to day submit and yield ourselves more unto thy
Majesty; preserve and increase thy Church, and destroy all the works of the devil and all false
and wicked counsels devised against thy holy word. Confound thine enemies by the might of thy
truth and righteousness, that so all power which exalteth itself against thine honour may from
day to day be more destroyed and brought to nought, until the perfection of thy kingdom come,
when thou shalt reveal thy glory in us at the last judgement and be all in all for ever.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-4"></a>R2.4 All estates / households

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588. *The rubric is in Kurpfalz 1563 only.*

**Rubric.** Thy will be done, etc.

**Prayer.** Grant also that we and all men may renounce our own will and all the lusts
of our flesh, and obey thy will, which alone is good, without any gainsaying; that so every man
may perform his office and calling as willingly and faithfully as the angels in heaven.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-5"></a>R2.5 Fruits of the earth

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588. *The rubric is in Kurpfalz 1563 only.*

**Rubric.** Give us this day our daily bread.

**Prayer.** Provide us also with all bodily necessaries, and vouchsafe us peace and
good government, that we may thereby acknowledge that thou art the only fountain of all good and
a faithful Father who careth for his children, and that without thy blessing neither our care
and labour nor thy gifts can prosper us; and that we may therefore withdraw our trust from all
creatures and set it upon thee alone.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-6"></a>R2.6 Repentance & forgiveness

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588. *The rubric is in Kurpfalz 1563 only.*

**Rubric.** Forgive us our debts, etc.

**Prayer.** Impute not unto us poor sinners all our misdeeds and debts, nor the evil
that yet always cleaveth unto us, for the sake of the shedding of the blood of Jesus Christ;
even as we also find this witness of thy grace in our hearts, that we forgive our neighbour from
the heart and desire to further his good.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-7"></a>R2.7 The present congregation

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588. *The rubric is in Kurpfalz 1563 only.*

**Rubric.** Lead us not into temptation, etc.

**Prayer.** And forasmuch as we of ourselves are so weak that we cannot stand one
moment, and moreover our sworn enemies, the devil, the world and our own flesh, cease not to
assail us: uphold and strengthen us by the power of thy Holy Spirit, that we may make firm
resistance against them and not be overcome in this spiritual warfare, but abide steadfast,
until at the last we obtain the victory perfectly and reign for ever in thy kingdom with thy
Son, our Lord and protector Jesus Christ.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-8"></a>R2.8 Conclusion

*Witnesses:* Kurpfalz 1563 and Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588.

**Prayer.** All which we ask of thee, that thereby not we but thou mayest be praised
for ever; and that thou canst do this as an almighty God, and wilt do it as a faithful Father,
as surely as we desire this of thee from the heart; through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen. Our
Father, etc.

#### <a id="s6-19-r2-9"></a>R2.9 Creed

*Witnesses:* Bentheim-Tecklenburg 1588.

**Prayer.** Give us also steadfastness and daily increase in the old, true and
undoubted Christian faith, that thereby we may make ourselves more and more partakers of Christ
Jesus and all his benefits; of which faith we make confession with mouth and heart, saying: I
believe in God the Father Almighty, etc.

---

### <a id="s6-20"></a>6.20 Family R3: Calvin’s “grande prière” (Strasbourg/Geneva)

Calvin's Strasbourg/Geneva "grande prière" in Latin, for the French refugee church, ending in a
paraphrase of the Lord's Prayer.

- **Earliest witness (archetype):** Frankfurt 1554 (Poullain).
- **Tradition:** Reformed.
- **Language:** Latin.
- **Form:** continuous prayer ending in a Lord's Prayer paraphrase.
- **Place in the service (Frankfurt 1554 (Poullain)):** Sunday morning: after the hour-long
  sermon and the announcements (betrothals, baptisms, the poor and sick who commend themselves to
  the prayers of the Church), while deacons collect alms at the door; followed immediately by the
  Creed, a psalm and the Aaronic blessing.

| Year | Witness | Territory | Sehling | Form |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1554 | Frankfurt, Liturgia sacra of the stranger congregation (Valérand Poullain) (Reformed) | Frankfurt am Main: French/Walloon refugee church | Sehling 9, VI/Frankfurt Nr. 14, pp. 563–566 | continuous prayer with Lord’s-Prayer paraphrase |

The words between asterisks in R3.8 are said only when the Supper is celebrated.

**Sequence:** R3.1 Special intercessions > R3.2 Exhortation / preface > R3.3 Civil authority >
R3.4 Ministers of the Word > R3.5 All men > R3.6 The afflicted > R3.7 The persecuted > R3.8 The
present congregation > R3.9 Lord's Prayer > R3.10 Creed.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-1"></a>R3.1 Special intercessions

**Rubric.** He endeth the sermon within the space of an hour and concludeth it with
the prayer subjoined. But first he admonisheth the Church of aught that is worthy or needful:
as, if there be betrothals, if a baptism, if any poor or sick man commend himself to the prayers
of the Church, and other things of the kind. Meanwhile two deacons at the door ask alms of every
one for the use of the poor.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-2"></a>R3.2 Exhortation / preface

**Rubric.** Prayer

**Prayer.** Almighty God, heavenly Father, thou hast promised to hear our petitions,
in whatsoever thing we call upon thee in the name of thy beloved Son Jesus Christ our Lord. He
also hath so taught us to hold holy assemblies among us in his name, inviting us moreover with
bountiful promises, that he will be in the midst of these our assemblies, that by him our only
Mediator and Intercessor we may obtain of thee whatsoever we shall ask with one accord upon
earth. And first of all thou commandest us to pray for all whom thou hast willed to be in
authority over us, and thereafter for those things that pertain to the needful uses of thy
people and of all men. Obeying this thy commandment, and trusting only in thy most holy
ordinance and thy promises, we are come together here before thee in the name of Christ thy Son
our Lord, humbly beseeching thee from the heart, O God and most good Father, in the name of our
only Deliverer and Mediator, that of thy clemency thou wouldest freely pardon us all our sins,
and so bend and draw unto thee our hearts, minds, thoughts and all our desires, that we may be
able to call upon thee with true and single prayer, which may be pleasing and acceptable unto
thee.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-3"></a>R3.3 Civil authority

**Prayer.** We pray therefore thy clemency, O heavenly Father, for princes and all men
bearing authority, thy servants, to whom it is committed of thee to do justice to thy people,
and by name for the consuls and senate of this city: that thou wouldest vouchsafe to bestow upon
them thy Spirit, which is truly a princely Spirit and the governor of wills, and increase more
and more from day to day his gifts, power and grace; that they may truly acknowledge the one and
only Christ thy Son our Lord, the King of kings, holding the principality above all power, to
whom indeed all power in heaven and in earth hath been given of thee; and then, being persuaded
with sure faith, may study with all their hearts to approve themselves unto him with true and
spiritual worship, and to advance and enlarge his kingdom among their subjects, whom also they
may rule according to the prescript of thy will out of thy law, as they surely know that both
they and these are made and fashioned of thee, and are the sheep of thy flocks. May it be
granted us therefore by thy benefit to enjoy peace, wherein we may serve thee in all holiness
and honesty, and, being delivered from our enemies, may render thee thanks and praises.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-4"></a>R3.4 Ministers of the Word

**Prayer.** We pray also, O true Father and only Deliverer, for those whom thou hast
given as pastors to thy Church, and to whom thou hast committed the care of the salvation of
souls and the ministry of thy most holy Gospel: so govern and help them by thy Spirit, that they
may be faithful ministers of thy glory, bending all their endeavours to this, that the flock of
thy sheep, yet wandering, may gather together into one unto Jesus Christ, the true and chief
Shepherd and Prince of bishops, that in him and through him they may grow more and more from day
to day in all righteousness and holiness of life. Vouchsafe again to deliver all thy churches
and to snatch them out of the jaws of the wolves and the claws of all hirelings, which serve
their own ambition and do all things for their own gain, caring for nothing less than that thy
most holy name be everywhere renowned and holy, and thy flock attain unto salvation.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-5"></a>R3.5 All men

**Prayer.** Moreover we beseech thee, O most clement God and merciful Father, for the
whole race of men: that as thou wilt be acknowledged of all throughout the whole world as the
only Deliverer, redemption having been wrought through Christ thy Son, thou wouldest vouchsafe
also to bring back into the right way of salvation, enlightened by thy Spirit through the
preaching of the Gospel, all that are yet this day far off from the same Christ thy Son, sitting
bound in darkness and in all ignorance of salvation; that they may know thee the true God, and
Jesus Christ whom thou hast sent. And them whom thou hast already vouchsafed that favour, that
thou hast shone into their minds by the manifestation of thy word, make them from day to day to
grow richer and more blessed in all good and in the abundance of thy spiritual blessing; that at
the last we may all be able with one accord truly and from the heart to adore thy Majesty and
extol it with praises, and finally to deliver ourselves wholly into the keeping of thine
Only-begotten, whom alone we acknowledge as our Lord, King and Lawgiver.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-6"></a>R3.6 The afflicted

**Prayer.** To these things we commend unto thee also, O God of comfort, those whom
thou visitest, that thou mayest chasten them with the cross or with any kind of affliction; and
the peoples whom thou now pressest with pestilence, war or famine; and lastly every one whom any
want sent by thee oppresseth, or prison, or sickness, or exile, or any calamity whatsoever, be
it of body or of mind. Grant that they may understand thy truly fatherly goodwill toward them,
namely that thou chastenest and correctest them to this end, that being amended they may return
unto thee with their whole heart, and, being delivered from all evils, may receive full
consolation.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-7"></a>R3.7 The persecuted

**Prayer.** But above all we would have commended unto thee our brethren, thine elect,
as many as yet live scattered under the tyranny of Antichrist, destitute of the food of
spiritual life and of that liberty of thy children, that they might publicly call upon thy name;
and first of all those that are in bonds or in any manner oppressed among the enemies of thy
Gospel. Vouchsafe, O most indulgent Father, to increase in them the strength of thy Spirit, that
they may be the firmer and never fail, but persevere constantly in thy holy calling. Be pleased
ever to uphold and stay them with thy help, so far as thou knowest to be needful, and withal to
comfort them in all adversities and defend them by thy care against the rage of the wolves, that
through them thy name may be made more glorious both in life and in death.

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-8"></a>R3.8 The present congregation

**Prayer.** Grant lastly, O God and Father, unto us that are now gathered together in
the name of Jesus Christ thy Son to hear the word of the Gospel \*and to communicate in the most
holy mysteries of his Supper\*, that we may truly acknowledge and earnestly feel how wretched
and lost we are even from our first origin, provoking thy judgement against us more and more
from day to day by the wickedness of our life; and so, when we have perceived how there is no
good in us, and that our flesh and blood can in no wise obtain the inheritance of thy kingdom,
we may give ourselves up with our whole hearts to thy only beloved Son Jesus Christ, our only
Deliverer, that he may so possess us and dwell in our hearts that, the old Adam being dead and
utterly done away, we may be renewed unto purity of life:

#### <a id="s6-20-r3-9"></a>R3.9 Lord's Prayer

**Rubric.** Paraphrase of the Lord’s Prayer, 1–6

**Prayer.** 1. whereby thy name, as is meet, may be extolled with praises above all
things everywhere and be made great. 2. That thou mayest also hold, yea, exercise thy right and
dominion over us all, that we may learn more and more from day to day to worship thy Majesty
with true obedience and due reverence; 3. and that thou alone mayest reign everywhere, the Lord
of all, and govern and rule thy people by the sceptre of thy word and the power of thy Spirit,
and overthrow all that oppose thee, vanquished by the might of thy truth and righteousness. So
shall it come to pass that all power and height that striveth against thy glory shall little by
little be destroyed and utterly overturned, until thy kingdom be made manifest, to wit, that
thou alone art King and Lord, who art to come to judgement. May we also with all creatures obey
thee in all things, as we know that the holy Angels, which dwell with thee in the heavens, will
have nothing else but that whatsoever is pleasing and acceptable unto thee be forthwith
performed without delay according to the pleasure of thy will; and may we so study to please
thee also, all the desires and pleasures of our flesh being neglected and set aside. 4. And so
long as we walk before thee with love and fear of thy name, do thou of thy goodness nourish and
feed us, supplying all things that be necessary for this life, that we may eat our bread in
peace, whereby through thy care and solicitude for us we may be most fully persuaded that thou
art the Father from whom alone all things are to be looked for, and, laying aside all trust in
ourselves and in all creatures, may rest in thy goodness and benevolence alone. 5. But forasmuch
as, so long as this life endureth, we miserable sinners are in the midst of death, and are so
frail that we continually slip and stumble at all things, and ever wandering depart from the
right: be thou in this behalf so propitious unto us, that thou pardon all these offences whereby
we have made ourselves liable to thy most just judgement, and by the same pardon deliver us from
eternal death, to which by our desert we are adjudged. Therefore impute not unto us this evil
that we carry about, even as we also by thy commandment forget injuries, and instead of revenge
pray for all good things for our enemies. 6. And finally, for the time to come uphold us by thy
power, lest, falling again through the infirmity of the flesh, we offend thee. And since such is
the weakness of our strength that we cannot stand firm even for a moment of time, and being
beset on every side with most cruel enemies we suffer continual assault from the devil, the
world and the flesh, with which we have perpetual war: strengthen us by thy Spirit and fortify
